22.6.10.a.s: etasyaiva vāyavyāsu pañcadaśamagniṣṭomasāma kṛtvāmayāvinamannādyakāmaṃ prajākāmaṃ paśukāmaṃ vā yājayet /
22.6.10.a.d: एतस्यैव वायव्यासु पञ्चदशमग्निष्टोमसाम कृत्वामयाविनमन्नाद्यकामं प्रजाकामं पशुकामं वा याजयेत् ।
22.6.10.a.m: Having made the fifteen-versed Agniṣṭoma chant of this very [rite] on verses to Vāyu, one should officiate for one who is chronically ill, one who desires food, one who desires offspring, or one who desires cattle;

22.6.10.b.m: having made the Vāravantīya the Agniṣṭoma chant of this very [rite] on Revatī verses, [one should officiate] for one who desires spiritual luster;

22.6.10.c.m: having made this very [rite] a Catuṣṭoma, [one should officiate] for one who desires a village.

22.6.11.a.m: Some say: they are without the Pravargya.

22.6.13.a.m: one desiring valor, with the fifteen-versed.

22.6.14.a.s: saptadaśenāgniṣṭutāgniṣṭomena yajñavibhraṣṭo yajeta yasminvā kratau vibhraṃśeta
22.6.14.a.d: सप्तदशेनाग्निष्टुताग्निष्टोमेन यज्ञविभ्रष्टो यजेत यस्मिन्वा क्रतौ विभ्रंशेत
22.6.14.a.m: One who has fallen away from sacrifice should sacrifice with the seventeen-versed Agniṣṭut Agniṣṭoma, or [he should sacrifice with it] in whatever rite he fell away.

22.6.15.a.m: The threefold is for one who speaks blame;

22.6.16.a.m: the fifteen-versed is prescribed for one guilty of killing;

22.6.17.a.m: the seventeen-versed is for one who has eaten uneatable food;

22.6.18.a.m: the twenty-one-versed is for one going among the people of Gandhāra, Kaliṅga, Magadha, Pāraskara, or Sauvīra;

22.6.20.a.m: one desiring heaven, with the thirty-three-versed.

22.6.21.a.m: [or] in the Agniṣṭoma, one may desire all desires.

22.7.1.a.m: There are four trivṛt Agniṣṭomas having the Rathaṃtara-sāman.

22.7.2.a.m: One who desires a village should sacrifice with the first of these, which is unexpressed (anirukta).

22.7.3.a.m: "The morning pressing is expressed (nirukta)," say some.

22.7.6.a.s: brāhmaṇo brahmavarcasakāmaḥ purodhākāmo vā yajeta yaṃ vā sthāpatyāyābhiṣiñceyuḥ
22.7.6.a.d: ब्राह्मणो ब्रह्मवर्चसकामः पुरोधाकामो वा यजेत यं वा स्थापत्यायाभिषिञ्चेयुः
22.7.6.a.m: A brahmin desiring brahmic luster, or desiring the office of purohita, or one whom they would consecrate to governorship (sthāpatya), should sacrifice [with it].

22.7.7.a.m: The hotṛ wears a garland, is reddish, blinking, and thrice-pure.

22.7.8.a.s: bṛhaspate juṣasva na iti bārhaspatyamatigrāhyaṃ gṛhṇāti
22.7.8.a.d: बृहस्पते जुषस्व न इति बार्हस्पत्यमतिग्राह्यं गृह्णाति
22.7.8.a.m: With "O Bṛhaspati, enjoy our...", he draws the Bārhaspatya atigrāhya draught.

22.7.9.a.m: An animal dedicated to Bṛhaspati is to be seized.

22.7.10.a.m: At the morning pressing, when the nārāśaṃsa goblets are deposited, he assigns eleven sacrificial gifts.

22.7.11.a.s: ājyena mādhyaṃdine savane kṛṣṇājina āsīnamabhiṣiñcati śukrāmanthinorvā saṃsrāveṇa bṛhaspate yuvamindraśca vasvo divyasyeśāthe uta pārthivasya /
22.7.11.a.d: आज्येन माध्यंदिने सवने कृष्णाजिन आसीनमभिषिञ्चति शुक्रामन्थिनोर्वा संस्रावेण बृहस्पते युवमिन्द्रश्च वस्वो दिव्यस्येशाथे उत पार्थिवस्य ।
22.7.11.a.m: At the midday pressing, he consecrates [the sacrificer] seated on a black antelope skin with clarified butter or with the residue of the Śukra and Manthin [draughts], with: "O Bṛhaspati, you two and Indra rule over divine wealth and earthly;

22.7.11.b.s: dhattaṃ rayiṃ stuvate kīraye cidyūyaṃ pāta svastibhiḥ sadā na iti
22.7.11.b.d: धत्तं रयिं स्तुवते कीरये चिद्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा न इति
22.7.11.b.m: give wealth to the praising singer; do you protect us always with well-being."

22.7.12.a.m: At the midday [pressing], [eleven cattle] together with a horse making twelve;

22.7.14.a.s: api vāṣṭau prātaḥsavana ekādaśa mādhyaṃdine dvādaśa tṛtīyasavane /
22.7.14.a.d: अपि वाष्टौ प्रातःसवन एकादश माध्यंदिने द्वादश तृतीयसवने ।
22.7.14.a.m: Or rather, eight at the morning pressing, eleven at the midday pressing, twelve at the third pressing;

22.7.15.a.m: They lead the horse at each pressing in three shares;

22.7.16.a.m: or rather, he should contemplate [it] with the mind at the other two pressings;

22.7.17.a.m: Having made the iṣu-viṣṭuti of the third, one should sacrifice while practicing sorcery.

22.7.18.a.m: The rest is identical with the Śyena.

22.7.20.a.m: The fourth is the Sarvasvāra, the Śunaskarṇastoma.

22.7.21.a.s: maraṇakāmo yajeta yaḥ kāmayetānāmayatā svargaṃ lokamiyāmiti
22.7.21.a.d: मरणकामो यजेत यः कामयेतानामयता स्वर्गं लोकमियामिति
22.7.21.a.m: One desiring death should sacrifice [with it], who desires, "May I go to the heavenly world free from disease."

22.7.22.a.m: An animal dedicated to Yama, parrot-green, is to be seized.

22.7.24.a.s: ārbhave stūyamāne dakṣiṇenaudumbarīṃ pattodaśenāhatena vāsasā dakṣiṇāśirāḥ prāvṛtaḥ saṃviśannāha brāhmaṇāḥ samāpayata me yajñamiti
22.7.24.a.d: आर्भवे स्तूयमाने दक्षिणेनौदुम्बरीं पत्तोदशेनाहतेन वाससा दक्षिणाशिराः प्रावृतः संविशन्नाह ब्राह्मणाः समापयत मे यज्ञमिति
22.7.24.a.m: While the Ārbhava-pavamāna is being chanted, lying down to the south of the udumbara post, wrapped with his head to the south in an unwashed garment with fringes at the feet, he says, "O brahmins, bring my sacrifice to completion!"

22.7.26.a.m: One desiring prosperity should sacrifice with the Bhuva-ukthya having the Rathaṃtara-sāman.

22.8.1.a.s: akṣayyaṃ ha vai cāturmāsyayājinaḥ sukṛtaṃ bhavati
22.8.1.a.d: अक्षय्यं ह वै चातुर्मास्ययाजिनः सुकृतं भवति
22.8.1.a.m: Imperishable indeed is the merit of one who sacrifices with the Cāturmāsya sacrifices.

22.8.2.a.m: In place of the Vaiśvadeva [offering], there is a trivṛt Agniṣṭoma.

22.8.3.b.m: the anūbandhyā cow is dedicated to Bṛhaspati.

22.8.4.a.m: Subsequent to the morning pressing oblations, he offers the Vaiśvadeva oblations.

22.8.5.a.m: The sviṣṭakṛt and iḍā offerings, however, are common.

22.8.6.b.m: they do not heap up the high altar (uttaravedi).

22.8.7.a.m: They bind the animal to an enclosing stick,

22.8.8.a.m: In the subsequent [sacrifices], they erect the sacrificial posts;

22.8.8.b.m: they heap up the high altar.

22.8.9.a.d: ततश्चतुर्षु मासेषु वरुणप्रघासानां लोके ऽग्निष्टोम उक्थ्यः ।
22.8.9.a.m: Then, after four months, in place of the Varuṇapraghāsa offerings, there is an Agniṣṭoma and an Ukthya;

22.8.10.c.m: the anūbandhyā cow is dedicated to Mitra and Varuṇa.

22.8.11.a.m: The oblations of the Varuṇapraghāsa offerings are [offered] like those of the Vaiśvadeva.

22.8.12.a.m: At the mārjālīya fire, they perform the ritual with the dishes of barley flour.

22.8.13.a.d: ततश्चतुर्षु मासेषु साकमेधानां लोके ऽग्निष्टोम उक्थ्यो ऽतिरात्रः
22.8.13.a.m: Then, after four months, in place of the Sākamedha offerings, there is an Agniṣṭoma, an Ukthya, and an Atirātra.

22.8.14.c.m: in the third, the eleven [animals of the ekādaśinī], or [an animal] dedicated to Prajāpati;

22.8.15.a.m: On the first day, [he offers the oblations] dedicated to Agni Anīkavat [subsequent to] the morning pressing oblations.

22.8.15.b.m: [The offerings of the] Sāṃtapana [belong] to the midday pressing.

22.8.16.a.m: When the Vasatīvarī waters have been carried around, they proceed with the Gṛhamedhīya [offering].

22.8.17.a.m: On the next day, after the morning litany has been commenced, they proceed with the full-ladle offering.

22.8.18.a.m: [The offerings of the] Krīḍin [Maruts belong] to the morning pressing;

22.8.18.b.m: [those of the] Svātavas [Maruts] to the midday pressing;

22.8.18.c.m: the great offering (Mahāhavis) to the third pressing.

22.8.19.a.s: sanneṣu nārāśaṃseṣu pariśrite mārjālīye pitṛyajñena caranti
22.8.19.a.d: सन्नेषु नाराशंसेषु परिश्रिते मार्जालीये पितृयज्ञेन चरन्ति
22.8.19.a.m: When the Nārāśaṃsa goblets have been placed down and the mārjālīya [shed] has been enclosed, they proceed with the Pitṛyajña.

22.8.20.a.m: Having performed the Traiyambaka offerings and returned, they proceed with the Āditya [offering].

22.9.1.a.m: Then, after four months, in the place of the Śunāsīrīya, [there is] a Jyotiragniṣṭoma.

22.9.3.a.m: The Śunāsīrīya offerings are like the Vaiśvadeva.

22.9.4.a.m: The intermediate vows are like those of the Cāturmāsya sacrifices.

22.9.5.a.m: Everywhere he emerges from the final bath wearing an unwashed garment.

22.9.6.a.m: Day after day he gives fifty cows as sacrificial gift;

22.9.7.a.m: Or [he gives gifts] according to each season, or respectively as in the Cāturmāsya sacrifices;

22.9.7.b.m: at the third pressing, [he gives] the calves along with their mothers.

22.9.8.a.m: One desiring a village should sacrifice with the Upahavya Agniṣṭoma performed indistinctly (anirukta).

22.9.9.a.m: Some say that the morning pressing is distinctly recited (nirukta).

22.9.11.a.m: One desiring heaven [should sacrifice] with the Ṛtapeya Agniṣṭoma having the Bṛhatsāman.

22.9.14.a.m: When the soma has been bought, the vow [food] is as much as the first finger-joint;

22.9.15.a.m: with each subsequent joint [in size] he undertakes the vow.

22.9.16.a.m: At night he sits facing the āhavanīya;

22.9.17.a.m: Having spoken truth, they glide forward;

22.9.17.b.m: speaking truth, they partake [of the soma].

22.9.18.a.s: audumbaraścamsaścatuḥsraktiḥ somasya pūrṇaḥ sagotrāya priyāya brahmaṇe deyaḥ
22.9.18.a.d: औदुम्बरश्चम्सश्चतुःस्रक्तिः सोमस्य पूर्णः सगोत्राय प्रियाय ब्रह्मणे देयः
22.9.18.a.m: A four-cornered goblet of udumbara wood, full of soma, should be given to a dear brahman priest of the same lineage.

22.9.19.a.m: With the Bahuhiraṇya Agniṣṭoma, one attains the realm of the draft ox and conquers radiant realms.

22.9.20.a.m: He gives twelve measures of gold at the consecration offering;

22.9.20.b.m: twice as much at the opening offering;

22.9.21.a.s: evamata ūrdhvaṃ dviguṇābhyāsenātithyāyāmupasatprayogeṣvagnīṣomīyasya vapāyāmagnīṣomīye savanīyasya vapāyāṃ savanīye prataḥsavane
22.9.21.a.d: एवमत ऊर्ध्वं द्विगुणाभ्यासेनातिथ्यायामुपसत्प्रयोगेष्वग्नीषोमीयस्य वपायामग्नीषोमीये सवनीयस्य वपायां सवनीये प्रतःसवने
22.9.21.a.m: in this manner, henceforth by doubling [each time]: at the guest offering, at the performances of the upasads, at the omentum of the Agnīṣomīya [victim], at the Agnīṣomīya [sacrifice], at the omentum of the animal for the pressing, at the animal for the pressing, and at the morning pressing.

22.9.22.a.m: When the Nārāśaṃsa goblets have been placed down, he gives an additional one hundred oxen.

22.10.1.a.s: hiraṇyasrajamudgātre ṣaṭpuṣkarāṃ dvādaśapuṣkarāṃ vā yajñāyajñīyasya stotre 'vabhṛtheṣṭyāmudayanīyāyāmanūbandhyāyāmudavasānīyāyāṃ ca
22.10.1.a.d: हिरण्यस्रजमुद्गात्रे षट्पुष्करां द्वादशपुष्करां वा यज्ञायज्ञीयस्य स्तोत्रे ऽवभृथेष्ट्यामुदयनीयायामनूबन्ध्यायामुदवसानीयायां च
22.10.1.a.m: He gives a golden garland having six lotuses, or having twelve lotuses, to the udgātṛ priest at the chant of the Yajñāyajñīya, at the final bath offering, at the concluding offering, at the barren cow offering, and at the departure offering.

22.10.2.a.m: A brahmin desiring spiritual splendour [should sacrifice] with the Trivṛt Agniṣṭut Agniṣṭoma having the Rathaṃtara-sāman.

22.10.3.a.m: A kṣatriya desiring valour [should sacrifice] with the fifteen-versed Indrastoma Ukthya having the Bṛhat-sāman.

22.10.4.a.m: A vaiśya desiring cattle [should sacrifice] with the seventeen-versed Agniṣṭut Agniṣṭoma having the Kaṇvarathaṃtara-sāman.

22.10.5.a.m: The morning pressing is performed with fresh warm milk, as has been said.

22.10.6.a.s: tīvrasutokthyena rathaṃtarasāmnā bṛhatsāmnobhayasāmnā vāmayāvinamannādyakāmaṃ prajākāmaṃ paśukāmaṃ śriyā vā pratyavarūḍhaṃ yājayet
22.10.6.a.d: तीव्रसुतोक्थ्येन रथंतरसाम्ना बृहत्साम्नोभयसाम्ना वामयाविनमन्नाद्यकामं प्रजाकामं पशुकामं श्रिया वा प्रत्यवरूढं याजयेत्
22.10.6.a.m: With the Tīvrasut Ukthya having the Rathaṃtara-sāman, having the Bṛhat-sāman, or having both sāmans, one should officiate for one who is chronically ill, one desiring proper food, one desiring offspring, one desiring cattle, or one who has fallen from prosperity.

22.10.9.a.m: The curds and other admixtures are as in the Vaiśyasava.

22.10.10.a.m: Or, with a boiled mixture at the third pressing.

22.10.12.a.m: the priests only smell [them], they do not partake [of them].

22.10.13.a.m: They partake of them at the chant of the acchāvāka priest.

22.10.14.a.m: The secondary hotṛ priests seek permission from the brahman priest.

22.10.15.a.m: Both adhvaryus and all camasādhvaryus respond to the acchāvāka.

22.10.16.a.m: A set of eleven stakes facing east is measured out.

22.10.17.a.m: He excavates the altar ground as far as the post.

22.10.18.a.m: A white pregnant mare is the sacrificial gift.

22.10.19.a.m: With the Marutstoma, a king and his domestic priest [achieve] union [with the deities].

22.10.20.b.s: yo rājyamāśaṃsamāno na labheta sa etena
22.10.20.b.d: यो राज्यमाशंसमानो न लभेत स एतेन
22.10.20.b.m: one who hopes for kingship but does not obtain it [should sacrifice] with this.

22.10.21.b.m: One who desires firm standing [sacrifices] with the Svarāj.

22.11.1.a.s: bahu pratigṛhya yo garagīriva manyeta sa punastomena /
22.11.1.a.d: बहु प्रतिगृह्य यो गरगीरिव मन्येत स पुनस्तोमेन ।
22.11.1.a.m: One who, having accepted much, considers himself as if poisoned, [sacrifices] with the Punastoma.

22.11.1.b.m: Or having eaten food that ought not to be eaten,

22.11.2.a.m: or having sacrificed for one for whom one ought not to sacrifice, say some.

22.11.3.a.m: One who is as if light [and] not established should [sacrifice] with this [sacrifice].

22.11.4.a.m: One who desires offspring [sacrifices] with the twenty-one-fold Upacchada.

22.11.5.a.m: At chant after chant, one stotrīyā-verse is added.

22.11.6.a.m: At the morning pressing, [with the formula:] “May the gandharvas and apsarases intoxicate [themselves]!"

22.11.7.a.m: when the nārāśaṃsa [goblets] have been deposited, he throws down a stalk [of soma] beneath the pūtabhṛt.

22.11.8.a.m: At the midday pressing, [with the formula:] “May the divine gandharvas intoxicate [themselves]!"

22.11.8.b.m: At the third pressing, [with the formula:] “May the ancestral gandharvas intoxicate [themselves]!"

22.11.10.a.m: At chant after chant, one stotrīyā-verse drops away.

22.11.11.a.m: “As it drops away, [the rival] drops away along with it,” so it is known [from sacred tradition].

22.11.12.a.m: One who desires, “May I become all this,” [sacrifices] with the Sarvatomukha.

22.11.13.b.m: In every direction are the soma-grounds.

22.11.14.a.m: The Rāśi and Arāyu catuṣṭomas belong to one who desires proper food.

22.11.15.a.m: At the former he gives a heap of grain [as dakṣiṇā].

22.11.16.a.m: One who desires cattle [sacrifices] with the two Gotamacatuṣṭomas.

22.11.17.a.m: The latter is an Ukthya with a Ṣoḍaśin.

22.11.19.a.m: One who desires cattle [sacrifices] with the Udbhid and Valabhid.

22.11.20.a.m: Having sacrificed with the Udbhid, he should sacrifice after a year with the Valabhid.

22.11.21.a.m: He undertakes the interval with an eight-pot-sherd [cake] for Agni.

22.11.22.a.m: In both cases, he gives full gāyatrī-gifts as dakṣiṇā:

22.12.2.a.m: One who desires respect [sacrifices] with the two Apacitis.

22.12.4.a.m: For them, a horse-drawn chariot with four yoked [horses] is the dakṣiṇā.

22.12.6.a.m: He [the sacrificer or sārathi] has gold ornaments, a trembling garland, all kinds of ornaments, and radiant rays.

22.12.7.a.s: tasya vaiyāghraḥ parivāro dvaipo dhanvadhirārkṣaḥ kavacaḥ
22.12.7.a.d: तस्य वैयाघ्रः परिवारो द्वैपो धन्वधिरार्क्षः कवचः
22.12.7.a.m: Its casing is of tiger-skin, the quiver of leopard-skin, the bow of bear-wood, and the armor [fitted].

22.12.8.a.m: The chariot-rider is armored, the charioteer is armored, enclosed by the two stationed [guards];

22.12.9.a.m: “the charioteer wears a gold breastplate and a wreath,” so it is known [from sacred tradition].

22.12.10.a.s: pakṣibhyāṃ sāgnicityābhyāṃ yaḥ kāmyeta pakṣī jyotiṣmataḥ svargāṃllokānanusaṃcareyamiti
22.12.10.a.d: पक्षिभ्यां साग्निचित्याभ्यां यः काम्येत पक्षी ज्योतिष्मतः स्वर्गांल्लोकाननुसंचरेयमिति
22.12.10.a.m: One who desires, “Becoming winged, may I wander over the radiant heavenly worlds,” [sacrifices] with the two winged [sacrifices] accompanied by the piling of the fire-altar.

22.12.11.a.s: ṛṣabheṇāgniṣṭomena rathaṃtarasāmnā rājānaṃ sāmgrāme saṃyatte yājayet
22.12.11.a.d: ऋषभेणाग्निष्टोमेन रथंतरसाम्ना राजानं साम्ग्रामे संयत्ते याजयेत्
22.12.11.a.m: With the Ṛṣabha Agniṣṭoma having the Rathaṃtara-sāman, he should sacrifice for a king engaged in battle.

22.12.12.a.m: Whatever they obtain there, from that one hundred and twelve [cows] are the dakṣiṇā.

22.12.14.a.m: Both the Bṛhat and Rathaṃtara [sāmans] are [used].

22.12.17.a.s: gosavena ṣaṭtriṃśenokthyena rathaṃtarasāmnā bṛhatsāmnobhayasāmnā vā svārājyakāmaḥ
22.12.17.a.d: गोसवेन षट्त्रिंशेनोक्थ्येन रथंतरसाम्ना बृहत्साम्नोभयसाम्ना वा स्वाराज्यकामः
22.12.17.a.m: One who desires independent rule [sacrifices] with the Gosava, a thirty-six-fold Ukthya having the Rathaṃtara-sāman, the Bṛhat-sāman, or both sāmans.

22.12.18.a.m: The Kaṇvarathaṃtara is at the pavamāna-chant.

22.12.20.a.s: dakṣiṇenāhavanīyamanuddhate vedyai bṛhataḥ stotraṃ pratyabhiṣicyate pratidhuṣā revajjātaḥ sahasā vṛddhaḥ kṣatrāṇāṃ kṣatrabhṛttamo vayodhāḥ /
22.12.20.a.d: दक्षिणेनाहवनीयमनुद्धते वेद्यै बृहतः स्तोत्रं प्रत्यभिषिच्यते प्रतिधुषा रेवज्जातः सहसा वृद्धः क्षत्राणां क्षत्रभृत्तमो वयोधाः ।
22.12.20.a.m: South of the āhavanīya on unraised ground of the altar ground, during the stotra of the Bṛhat, he is consecrated with fresh warm milk [with the verse:] “Born with wealth, grown with might, best bearer of royal power among rulers, bestower of strength;

22.12.20.b.s: mahānmahitve tastabhānaḥ kṣatre rāṣṭre ca jāgṛhi /
22.12.20.b.d: महान्महित्वे तस्तभानः क्षत्रे राष्ट्रे च जागृहि ।
22.12.20.b.m: firmly supported in great majesty, watch over the royal power and the realm!

22.12.20.c.m: I consecrate you with the independent rule of Prajāpati Parameṣṭhin.”

22.13.1.a.m: Having sacrificed with it, he observes the vow of a beast for a year.

22.13.2.a.m: Bending down, he should drink water, and he should crop grass;

22.13.2.b.m: he may approach his mother, he may approach his sister, he may approach a female of the same lineage;

22.13.3.a.m: wherever excretion overtakes him, there he should void [it].

22.13.4.a.m: With the Marutstoma one wins endless fortune.

22.13.5.a.m: With this he should sacrifice for two or three [persons].

22.13.6.a.m: The two Kulāyas of Agni belong to one who desires proper food.

22.13.7.a.m: The two Kulāya sacrifices of Indra and Agni are for one desiring heaven.

22.13.8.a.m: With the Indrastuta or Indrastoma, an Ukthya with the Bṛhat-sāman, a nobleman [sacrifices] desiring heroic power.

22.13.10.a.m: With the stoma of Indra and Agni, he should sacrifice for both the king and the royal priest, sharing a single prosperity.

22.13.11.a.m: Brilliance and spiritual luster [accrue] to the brāhmaṇa;

22.13.12.a.m: With the Vighana he destroys evil and his rival;

22.13.12.b.m: with it he destroys all enemies.

22.13.13.a.m: With the Vajra Ṣoḍaśin, [one sacrifices] when performing sorcery;

22.13.14.a.m: For both of them, the ritual procedure is explained by the Śyena.

22.13.17.a.m: With the Sarvastoma, one wishing to become prosperous [sacrifices].

22.13.19.a.m: With the Aptoryāma, for one from whom cattle would tend to fall away;

22.13.19.b.m: he obtains everything, he conquers everything.

22.13.20.a.m: With the Navasaptadaśa, [one sacrifices] desiring offspring.

22.13.21.a.m: With the Viṣuvat, the son of the eldest wife [sacrifices];

22.13.25.a.m: With the Viśvajit, one who has rivals [sacrifices].

22.13.27.a.m: With the Pañcadaśa, [one sacrifices] desiring heroic power.

22.13.28.a.m: With the Saptadaśa, [one sacrifices] desiring offspring.

22.13.29.a.m: With the Ekaviṃśa, [one sacrifices] desiring a firm footing.

22.14.1.a.m: The ahīna sacrifices, beginning with the two-day sacrifice and ending with the eleven-day sacrifice, have an Atirātra at the end.

22.14.2.a.m: Their ritual procedure is explained by the Dvādaśāha in its form as an ahīna.

22.14.3.a.m: Of the two-day sacrifice, the first day begins with the Aindravāyava cup, the subsequent [day] begins with the Śukra cup.

22.14.4.a.m: Of the three-day sacrifice, this same [order applies], and [the third day] begins with the Āgrayaṇa cup.

22.14.5.a.m: Of the four-day sacrifice, this same [order applies], and [the fourth day] begins with the Aindravāyava cup.

22.14.6.a.m: Of the five-day sacrifice, this same [order applies], and [the fifth day] begins with the Śukra cup.

22.14.7.a.m: In the six-day sacrifice, [the series] recurs twice.

22.14.8.a.m: Of the seven-day sacrifice, this same [order applies], and [the seventh day] begins with the Aindravāyava cup.

22.14.9.a.m: Of the eight-day sacrifice, this same [order applies], and [the eighth day] begins with the Śukra cup.

22.14.10.a.m: In the nine-day sacrifice, [the series] recurs three times.

22.14.11.a.m: Of the ten-day sacrifice, this same [order applies], and [the tenth day] begins with the Aindravāyava cup.

22.14.12.a.m: Of the eleven-day sacrifice, this same [order applies], and [the eleventh day] begins with the Śukra cup.

22.14.13.a.m: In the twelve-day sacrifice, [the series] recurs four times.

22.14.14.a.m: The drawing of the Ṣoḍaśin cup takes place on the later day of the two-day sacrifice.

22.14.15.a.m: It should be drawn on the middle [day] of the three-day sacrifice,

22.14.15.b.m: and on every fourth day in the various ahīnas beginning with the four-day sacrifice.

22.14.18.a.s: āṅgīrasena yaḥ puṇyo hīna iva syāt sa etena
22.14.18.a.d: आङ्गीरसेन यः पुण्यो हीन इव स्यात् स एतेन
22.14.18.a.m: With the Āṅgīrasa [dvirātra], one who is virtuous but feels as though deficient [sacrifices] with this.

22.14.19.a.m: The earlier [day] is a Jyotiṣṭoma Agniṣṭoma;

22.14.19.b.m: the later is a Sarvastoma Atirātra.

22.14.20.a.s: kāpivanena yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayate tamabhyaśnute 'lūkṣo bhavati
22.14.20.a.d: कापिवनेन यं कामं कामयते तमभ्यश्नुते ऽलूक्षो भवति
22.14.20.a.m: With the Kāpivana [dvirātra], he attains whichever wish he desires; he becomes unimpoverished.

22.14.21.a.m: The earlier [day] is a Jyotis Ukthya or Agniṣṭoma;

22.14.22.a.m: With the Caitraratha [dvirātra], he finds a firm footing in vital breaths and in proper food.

22.15.1.a.s: gargatrirātreṇa prajātiṃ bhūmānaṃ gacchatyabhi svargaṃ lokaṃ jayatyeṣu lokeṣu pratitiṣṭhati vasūnrukrānādityānanvārohati
22.15.1.a.d: गर्गत्रिरात्रेण प्रजातिं भूमानं गच्छत्यभि स्वर्गं लोकं जयत्येषु लोकेषु प्रतितिष्ठति वसून्रुक्रानादित्यानन्वारोहति
22.15.1.a.m: With the Garga three-day sacrifice, he attains offspring and abundance, conquers the heavenly world, finds a firm footing in these worlds, and ascends to the Vasus, Rudras, and Ādityas.

22.15.2.a.m: The Traidhātavīyā is the consecratory offering.

22.15.3.a.s: rohiṇī babhrurvā piṅgalaikahāyanī dvihāyani vā somakrayaṇī
22.15.3.a.d: रोहिणी बभ्रुर्वा पिङ्गलैकहायनी द्विहायनि वा सोमक्रयणी
22.15.3.a.m: The soma-purchasing cow is red or reddish-brown, tawny, one year old or two years old.

22.15.5.a.m: The pṛṣṭha stotras are the Rathaṃtara, Vāmadevya, and Bṛhat.

22.15.7.a.s: trīṇi śatāni trayastriṃśataṃ ca prathame 'hani dadāti /
22.15.7.a.d: त्रीणि शतानि त्रयस्त्रिंशतं च प्रथमे ऽहनि ददाति ।
22.15.7.a.m: On the first day he gives three hundred and thirty-three.

22.15.8.a.m: The thousandth [cow] remains over: red, speckle-spotted, of two colors, [or] black-and-white on both sides or on one side.

22.15.9.a.m: It is said: "whichever is the chosen, beautiful one."

22.15.10.a.m: On the first day, the prominent [animal given] is one having protruding horns.

22.15.11.a.m: He addresses it: "O Agni, bring the thousand; you split the hide of Vala.

22.15.11.b.s: sa naḥ sahasramā naya prajayā paśubhiḥ saha punarmā viśatādriyiriti
22.15.11.b.d: स नः सहस्रमा नय प्रजया पशुभिः सह पुनर्मा विशताद्रियिरिति
22.15.11.b.m: Do you bring to us the thousand, together with offspring and cattle; let wealth enter me again."

22.15.13.a.s: tāmabhimantrayate tvamapāmoṣadhīnāṃ rasena rasinī babhūvitha sā mā sahasra ā bhaja prajayā paśubhiḥ saha punarmā viśatādriyiriti
22.15.13.a.d: तामभिमन्त्रयते त्वमपामोषधीनां रसेन रसिनी बभूविथ सा मा सहस्र आ भज प्रजया पशुभिः सह पुनर्मा विशताद्रियिरिति
22.15.13.a.m: He addresses her: "Through the sap of the waters [and] of the plants you have become full of sap; do you grant me a share in the thousand, together with offspring and cattle; let wealth enter me again."

22.15.15.a.m: He addresses him: "You are the foundation of the thousand, you are the dwarf sacred to Viṣṇu.

22.15.15.b.s: sa naḥ sahasra ā dhehi prajayā paśubhiḥ saha punarmā viśatādrayiriti
22.15.15.b.d: स नः सहस्र आ धेहि प्रजया पशुभिः सह पुनर्मा विशताद्रयिरिति
22.15.15.b.m: Do you place us in the thousand, together with offspring and cattle; let wealth enter me again."

22.15.16.a.m: It has been said: "to the north of the āgnīdhra [he should lead her]."

22.16.1.a.s: dakṣiṇena vā vediṃ nītvāntarā yūpamāhavanīyaṃ ca droṇakalaśamavadhrāpayedā jighra kalaśamiti /
22.16.1.a.d: दक्षिणेन वा वेदिं नीत्वान्तरा यूपमाहवनीयं च द्रोणकलशमवध्रापयेदा जिघ्र कलशमिति ।
22.16.1.a.m: Or having led [her] to the south of the altar ground, between the sacrificial post and the āhavanīya, he should make her sniff the droṇakalaśa with: "Smell the vat."

22.16.1.b.m: [This takes place] at the āgnīdhra or at the havirdhāna shed.

22.16.2.a.m: Having led her northward to the āgnīdhra, he places a tārpya garment upon her back.

22.16.3.a.m: On it the form of the dhiṣṇya hearths is woven.

22.16.4.a.m: Then, while she stands facing west in front [of the fires], he should offer with: "Both of you have conquered..."

22.16.5.a.m: He offers the forms that are on her.

22.16.6.a.m: Some hand down [here the verses] belonging to the Aśvamedha.

22.16.7.a.s: pratīcīṃ sadasaḥ sraktimānīya tasyā upotthāya dakṣiṇaṃ karṇamājapediḍe ranta iti
22.16.7.a.d: प्रतीचीं सदसः स्रक्तिमानीय तस्या उपोत्थाय दक्षिणं कर्णमाजपेदिडे रन्त इति
22.16.7.a.m: Having brought her to the western corner of the sadas [hall], having stepped up close to her, he should whisper into her right ear: "O Iḍā, Rantā..."

22.16.8.a.m: Having released her, he attends to the omen:

22.16.9.a.s: yadyapuruṣābhivītā prācīyādarātsīdayaṃ yajamānaḥ kalyāṇaṃ lokamajaiṣīditi vidyāt /
22.16.9.a.d: यद्यपुरुषाभिवीता प्राचीयादरात्सीदयं यजमानः कल्याणं लोकमजैषीदिति विद्यात् ।
22.16.9.a.m: If, unprompted by men, she should go eastward, he should know: "This sacrificer has succeeded, he has won a good world."

22.16.9.b.m: If southward: "He will quickly depart from this world."

22.16.9.c.m: If westward: "He will have much grain."

22.16.9.d.m: If northward: "He will be superior in this world."

22.16.10.a.s: tāṃ yajamāno 'bhimantrayate sā mā suvargaṃ lokaṃ gamayeti
22.16.10.a.d: तां यजमानो ऽभिमन्त्रयते सा मा सुवर्गं लोकं गमयेति
22.16.10.a.m: The sacrificer addresses her: "Do you cause me to reach the heavenly world."

22.16.11.a.s: yāstisrastisrastriṃśatyadhi tāsvenāmupasamāhṛtya tāmagnīdhe brahmaṇe hotra udgātra unnetre 'dhvaryave vā dadyāt
22.16.11.a.d: यास्तिस्रस्तिस्रस्त्रिंशत्यधि तास्वेनामुपसमाहृत्य तामग्नीधे ब्रह्मणे होत्र उद्गात्र उन्नेत्रे ऽध्वर्यवे वा दद्यात्
22.16.11.a.m: Having united her with the three [cows] that are over and above the thirty [on each of the three days], he should give her to the agnīdh, to the brahman, to the hotṛ, to the udgātṛ, to the unnetṛ, or to the adhvaryu.

22.16.12.a.s: dvau vonnetārau vṛtvā yataro nāśrāvayettasmai vā
22.16.12.a.d: द्वौ वोन्नेतारौ वृत्वा यतरो नाश्रावयेत्तस्मै वा
22.16.12.a.m: Or, having chosen two unnetṛs, [he should give her] to whichever does not make the ritual call.

22.16.13.a.m: Or two shares to the brahman [and] a third to the agnīdh.

22.16.15.a.m: Or, after being driven out, she should roam at will.

22.16.15.b.m: It has been said: "Whoever receives her without knowing [her ritual meaning]..."

22.16.16.a.s: tāṃ śatamānena hiraṇyena niṣkrīya yajamānasya goṣṭhe visṛjati
22.16.16.a.d: तां शतमानेन हिरण्येन निष्क्रीय यजमानस्य गोष्ठे विसृजति
22.16.16.a.m: Having redeemed her with gold of a hundred mānas' [weight], he releases her into the cow-pen of the sacrificer.

22.17.1.a.m: They milk ten [cows] for the milk-admixture on the first day;

22.17.2.a.m: Cooked food is to be given on the first day;

22.17.2.b.m: gold, a cow, [and] a garment on the second;

22.17.2.c.s: ano ratho 'śvo hastī puruṣa iti tṛtīye
22.17.2.c.d: अनो रथो ऽश्वो हस्ती पुरुष इति तृतीये
22.17.2.c.m: a cart, a chariot, a horse, an elephant, [and] a slave on the third.

22.17.3.a.m: He should not give anything over and above the thousand [cows].

22.17.5.a.s: yadi dadyādanūbandhyāvapāyāṃ hutāyāṃ dakṣiṇā nayannnanyūnā daśato nayet
22.17.5.a.d: यदि दद्यादनूबन्ध्यावपायां हुतायां दक्षिणा नयन्न्नन्यूना दशतो नयेत्
22.17.5.a.m: If he should give, when the omentum of the anūbandhyā cow has been offered, leading the sacrificial gifts, he should not lead less than a decade.

22.17.6.a.m: To whomever he intends to give one cow, to ten of those he should present the tenth;

22.17.8.a.m: In this manner up to a hundred or up to a thousand.

22.17.9.a.m: Having led out the final sacrificial gift, or having performed the final leaving-rite, [he performs] the Śabalī [rite].

22.17.10.a.s: samudro 'si viśvavyacā brahmā devānāṃ prathamajā ṛtasya /
22.17.10.a.d: समुद्रो ऽसि विश्वव्यचा ब्रह्मा देवानां प्रथमजा ऋतस्य ।
22.17.10.a.m: "You are the ocean, all-encompassing, the Brahman of the gods, the first-born of truth.

22.17.10.b.m: You are food, you are seed, you are light, you are immortality.

22.17.10.c.m: We know you, O Śabalī, shining brightly.

22.17.10.d.s: tasyāste pṛthivī pādo 'ntarikṣaṃ pādo dyauḥ pādaḥ samudraḥ pādaḥ /
22.17.10.d.d: तस्यास्ते पृथिवी पादो ऽन्तरिक्षं पादो द्यौः पादः समुद्रः पादः ।
22.17.10.d.m: Of that you, the earth is a foot, the atmosphere is a foot, heaven is a foot, the ocean is a foot.

22.17.10.e.s: eṣāsi śabali tāṃ tvā vidma sā na iṣamūrjaṃ dhukṣva vasordhārāṃ śabali prajānāṃ śaviṣṭhā vrajamanugeṣaṃ svāheti śabalihomaṃ juhoti
22.17.10.e.d: एषासि शबलि तां त्वा विद्म सा न इषमूर्जं धुक्ष्व वसोर्धारां शबलि प्रजानां शविष्ठा व्रजमनुगेषं स्वाहेति शबलिहोमं जुहोति
22.17.10.e.m: This you are, O Śabalī; as such we know you; do you yield us vigor and nourishment, a stream of wealth, O Śabalī, most mighty among creatures; may I follow the cow-pen, svāhā"—with this he offers the Śabalihoma.

22.18.1.a.m: The [three days] of the Aśvamedha are Agniṣṭoma, Ukthya, [and] Atirātra.

22.18.2.a.m: The pṛṣṭha stotras are the Rathaṃtara, the Mahānāmnī, and the Bṛhat.

22.18.3.a.s: rājā yajeta yaḥ kāmayeta sarvamidaṃ bhaveyamiti
22.18.3.a.d: राजा यजेत यः कामयेत सर्वमिदं भवेयमिति
22.18.3.a.m: A king who desires: "May I become all this," should sacrifice [with it].

22.18.4.a.m: With the Baida three-day sacrifice, [one sacrifices] desiring independent rule.

22.18.5.a.m: There are three nine-versed Atirātras containing the Ṣoḍaśin.

22.18.6.a.m: The pṛṣṭha [chants] are Rathaṃtara, Vāmadevya, and Bṛhat.

22.18.7.a.m: By means of the Garga trirātra, the days and the pṛṣṭha [chants] of the subsequent three have been explained.

22.18.8.a.m: One who desires cattle [sacrifices] with the Chandomapavamāna.

22.18.9.a.m: By means of the Antarvasu, he obtains cattle.

22.18.13.a.d: चत्वारो ऽस्य वीराः कुल आजायन्ते सुहोतेत्युक्तम्
22.18.13.a.m: Four heroes are born in his family: "Suhotā..." has been stated.

22.18.14.a.m: There are an Agniṣṭoma, two Ukthyas, and an Atirātra; these are Atri's four catuṣṭomas.

22.18.16.a.m: One who desires prosperity [sacrifices] with the Jāmadagnya rite.

22.18.17.a.m: The upasads are accompanied by cakes.

22.18.18.a.s: āgneya ekakapāla āśvino dvikapālo vaiṣṇavatrikapālaḥ saumyaścatuṣkapālaḥ sāvitraḥ pañcakapālo dhātraḥ ṣaṭkapālo mārutaḥ saptakapālo bārhaspatyo 'ṣṭākapālo maitro navakapālo vāruṇo daśakapāla aindra ekādaśakapālo vaiśvadevo dvādaśakapālaḥ
22.18.18.a.d: आग्नेय एककपाल आश्विनो द्विकपालो वैष्णवत्रिकपालः सौम्यश्चतुष्कपालः सावित्रः पञ्चकपालो धात्रः षट्कपालो मारुतः सप्तकपालो बार्हस्पत्यो ऽष्टाकपालो मैत्रो नवकपालो वारुणो दशकपाल ऐन्द्र एकादशकपालो वैश्वदेवो द्वादशकपालः
22.18.18.a.m: [There are] a cake on one potsherd for Agni, on two potsherds for the Aśvins, on three potsherds for Viṣṇu, on four potsherds for Soma, on five potsherds for Savitṛ, on six potsherds for Dhātṛ, on seven potsherds for the Maruts, on eight potsherds for Bṛhaspati, on nine potsherds for Mitra, on ten potsherds for Varuṇa, on eleven potsherds for Indra, and on twelve potsherds for the Viśvedevas.

22.19.1.a.s: agne verhotraṃ veradhvaramā pitaraṃ vaiśvānaramavase karindrāya devebhyo juṣatāṃ haviḥ svāhā /
22.19.1.a.d: अग्ने वेर्होत्रं वेरध्वरमा पितरं वैश्वानरमवसे करिन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुषतां हविः स्वाहा ।
22.19.1.a.m: "O Agni, accept the hotṛ's office, accept the solemn ritual! Bring Father Vaiśvānara to help! For Indra, for the gods, let the oblation be relished! Svāhā!"

22.19.1.b.m: "O divine Aśvins, sprinkle with the honey-whip today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer!"

22.19.1.c.m: "O divine Viṣṇu, stride widely today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer!"

22.19.1.d.m: "O divine Soma, be the bestower of seed today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer!"

22.19.1.e.m: "O divine Savitṛ, impel good impelling today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer!"

22.19.1.f.m: "O divine Dhātṛ, be a good creator today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer!"

22.19.1.g.s: devā grāvāṇo madhumatīmadyāsminyajñe yajamānāya vācaṃ vadata /
22.19.1.g.d: देवा ग्रावाणो मधुमतीमद्यास्मिन्यज्ञे यजमानाय वाचं वदत ।
22.19.1.g.m: "O divine pressing-stones, speak sweet speech today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer!"

22.19.1.h.m: "O divine Aditi, follow along today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer!"

22.19.1.i.m: "O divine Anumati, approve today this sacrifice for the sacrificer!"

22.19.1.j.m: "O heavenly waters, bow down today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer!"

22.19.1.k.m: "To each assembly hall, possessing offspring, the Ṛbhu taking pleasure..."

22.19.1.l.m: "O divine Indra, be power today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer!"

22.19.1.m.s: deva tvaṣṭaḥ suretodhā adyāsminyajñe yajamānāyaidhīti pratinigadya homāḥ
22.19.1.m.d: देव त्वष्टः सुरेतोधा अद्यास्मिन्यज्ञे यजमानायैधीति प्रतिनिगद्य होमाः
22.19.1.m.m: "O divine Tvaṣṭṛ, be a good bestower of seed today in this sacrifice for the sacrificer!"—having recited [each formula] respectively, the oblations [are made].

22.19.2.a.s: indrāya devebhyo juṣatāṃ haviḥ svāheti sarvatrānuṣajati
22.19.2.a.d: इन्द्राय देवेभ्यो जुषतां हविः स्वाहेति सर्वत्रानुषजति
22.19.2.a.m: He attaches everywhere: "For Indra, for the gods, let the oblation be relished! Svāhā!"

22.20.1.b.s: yaḥ puṇyo hīna iva syātsa etena
22.20.1.b.d: यः पुण्यो हीन इव स्यात्स एतेन
22.20.1.b.m: He who is virtuous but feels deprived should sacrifice with this.

22.20.4.a.m: "The year, verily, was this one alone..." has been stated.

22.20.6.a.m: Whatever desire he desires, he attains it.

22.20.7.a.m: [Its days are:] an Agniṣṭoma, three Ukthyas, and an Atirātra.

22.20.8.a.m: Two pressings are trivṛt, one is pañcadaśa.

22.20.8.b.m: Two are pañcadaśa, one is saptadaśa.

22.20.8.c.m: Two are saptadaśa, one is ekaviṃśa.

22.20.8.d.m: Two are ekaviṃśa, one is triṇava.

22.20.8.e.m: Two are triṇava, one is trayastriṃśa.

22.20.9.a.m: By means of the Pañcaśāradīya, one becomes greater than the many.

22.20.10.a.m: Every year he sacrifices with an animal sacrifice.

22.20.11.a.m: They bring seventeen dapple-grey five-year-old oxen,

22.20.11.b.m: and seventeen dapple-grey three-year-old unbred heifers.

22.20.12.a.m: Having sprinkled the oxen and carried fire around them, they release them;

22.20.14.a.m: Having immolated striped ones, butter-spotted ones, reddish ones, yellowish-brown ones, and at last multi-colored ones, they undergo consecration.

22.20.15.a.s: trivṛdagniṣṭomaḥ pañcadaśa ukthyaḥ saptadaśa ukthyaḥ pañcadaśa ukthyaḥ saptadaśo 'tirātraḥ
22.20.15.a.d: त्रिवृदग्निष्टोमः पञ्चदश उक्थ्यः सप्तदश उक्थ्यः पञ्चदश उक्थ्यः सप्तदशो ऽतिरात्रः
22.20.15.a.m: A trivṛt Agniṣṭoma, a pañcadaśa Ukthya, a saptadaśa Ukthya, a pañcadaśa Ukthya, and a saptadaśa Atirātra [constitute the five days].

22.20.19.a.m: If Rudra should afflict the oxen,

22.21.1.a.m: he should offer a cake on eight potsherds to Agni associated with Rudra.

22.21.2.a.m: [He should offer] a mess of boiled rice sacred to Apāṃ Napāt, if [the ox] should fall into water.

22.21.3.a.m: A mess of boiled rice sacred to Nirṛti, if it should sink down.

22.21.4.a.s: bhaumaṃ carumekakapālaṃ vā yadyavasannaḥ saṃśīrṇo vā
22.21.4.a.d: भौमं चरुमेककपालं वा यद्यवसन्नः संशीर्णो वा
22.21.4.a.m: A mess of boiled rice sacred to Bhūmi, or a cake on one potsherd, if it has sunk down or is broken up.

22.21.5.a.s: bārhaspatyaṃ caruṃ yadi śloṇaḥ kūṭo vā
22.21.5.a.d: बार्हस्पत्यं चरुं यदि श्लोणः कूटो वा
22.21.5.a.m: A mess of boiled rice sacred to Bṛhaspati, if it is lame or hornless.

22.21.6.a.m: If it should be lost, a mess of boiled rice sacred to Vāyu.

22.21.7.a.m: If an invading army should seize [it], a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra the Conqueror.

22.21.8.a.m: If they should carry it off by force, a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra the Forceful.

22.21.9.a.m: If it should become blind, a mess of boiled rice sacred to Sūrya, or a cake on one potsherd.

22.21.10.a.m: If it should fall into a pit, a mess of boiled rice sacred to Viṣṇu.

22.21.11.a.s: yadyavijñātena yakṣmaṇā mriyeta prājāpatyaṃ caruṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ vā
22.21.11.a.d: यद्यविज्ञातेन यक्ष्मणा म्रियेत प्राजापत्यं चरुं द्वादशकपालं वा
22.21.11.a.m: If it should die of an unknown disease, a mess of boiled rice sacred to Prajāpati, or a cake on twelve potsherds.

22.21.12.a.m: The fourth [four-day rite] has the Mahāvrata within.

22.21.14.a.s: trivṛdagniṣṭomaḥ pañcadaśa ukthyo mahāvrataṃ saptadaśa ukthya ekaviṃśo 'tirātraḥ
22.21.14.a.d: त्रिवृदग्निष्टोमः पञ्चदश उक्थ्यो महाव्रतं सप्तदश उक्थ्य एकविंशो ऽतिरात्रः
22.21.14.a.m: A Trivṛt Agniṣṭoma, a Pañcadaśa Ukthya, the Mahāvrata [as] a Saptadaśa Ukthya, and an Ekaviṃśa Atirātra.

22.21.16.a.m: The days are like [those of] the Pañcaśāradīya.

22.21.17.a.m: He gives ten thousand on the first day,

22.21.17.c.m: a hundred million and a thousand million on the third.

22.21.17.d.m: As on the first two [days], so on the latter two.

22.22.3.a.m: "The Sādhyas were indeed gods desirous of heaven," as has been said.

22.22.4.a.m: One desirous of offspring [should sacrifice] with the second, [that] of the seasons.

22.22.6.a.m: With the third, which has the Trikadruka days following it, he attains whatever desire he desires.

22.22.7.a.s: trivṛdagniṣṭomaḥ pañcadaśa ukthyaḥ saptadaśa ukthyo jyotirgaurāyuratirātraḥ
22.22.7.a.d: त्रिवृदग्निष्टोमः पञ्चदश उक्थ्यः सप्तदश उक्थ्यो ज्योतिर्गौरायुरतिरात्रः
22.22.7.a.m: A Trivṛt Agniṣṭoma, a Pañcadaśa Ukthya, a Saptadaśa Ukthya, Jyotis, Go, Āyus, and an Atirātra.

22.22.8.a.m: With the fourth, he indeed propagates with offspring and cattle.

22.22.9.a.m: An Abhyāsaṅgya five-day rite and a Viśvajit Atirātra.

22.22.11.a.m: One desirous of cattle [should sacrifice] with the Kausurubinda.

22.22.13.a.m: One desirous of heaven [should sacrifice] with the second, [that] of the Seven Seers.

22.22.14.a.m: A Pṛṣṭhya-six-day rite and an Atirātra possessing the Mahāvrata.

22.22.15.a.m: One desirous of offspring [should sacrifice] with the Prājāpatya.

22.22.16.a.m: A Pṛṣṭhya-six-day rite, and the Prājāpatya Mahāvrata on an Atirātra.

22.22.17.a.m: One desirous of cattle [should sacrifice] with the Chandomapavamāna.

22.22.18.a.m: A Pṛṣṭhya-six-day rite, and the Chandomapavamāna Mahāvrata on an Atirātra.

22.22.19.a.m: One desirous of food [should sacrifice] with the Pṛṣṭhyāvalamba.

22.22.20.a.m: A Pṛṣṭhyastoma-six-day rite and an Atirātra possessing the Mahāvrata.

22.23.1.a.m: One desirous of food [should sacrifice] with the Sattrasaṃmita.

22.23.2.a.m: The days are like [those of] the Kausurubinda.

22.23.4.a.m: Jyotis, Go, Āyus, then Abhijit, Viśvajit, Sarvajit, and a Sarvastoma Atirātra.

22.23.5.a.s: janakasaptarātreṇa prajātiṃ bhūmānaṃ gacchatyabhi svargaṃ lokaṃ jayatyeṣu lokeṣu pratitiṣṭhati
22.23.5.a.d: जनकसप्तरात्रेण प्रजातिं भूमानं गच्छत्यभि स्वर्गं लोकं जयत्येषु लोकेषु प्रतितिष्ठति
22.23.5.a.m: With the Janakasaptarātra he attains progeny and abundance, conquers the heavenly world, and is firmly established in these worlds.

22.23.6.a.d: चत्वारि त्रिवृन्त्यहान्यग्निष्टोममुखानि विश्वजिन्महाव्रतं ज्योतिष्टोमो वैश्वानरो ऽतिरात्रः
22.23.6.a.m: Four Trivṛt days beginning with an Agniṣṭoma, a Viśvajit, a Mahāvrata, and a Jyotiṣṭoma Vaiśvānara Atirātra.

22.23.7.a.m: One desirous of spiritual lustre [should sacrifice] with the eight-day rite.

22.23.10.a.m: A Pṛṣṭhya-six-day rite, Jyotis, Go, Āyus, and an Atirātra.

22.23.11.a.m: One desirous of spiritual lustre [should sacrifice] with the second.

22.23.12.a.s: trivṛdagniṣṭomaḥ pañcadaśa ukthyaḥ sapatadaśa ukthyo 'bhyāsaṅgyaḥ pañcāho viśvajidatirātraḥ
22.23.12.a.d: त्रिवृदग्निष्टोमः पञ्चदश उक्थ्यः सपतदश उक्थ्यो ऽभ्यासङ्ग्यः पञ्चाहो विश्वजिदतिरात्रः
22.23.12.a.m: A Trivṛt Agniṣṭoma, a Pañcadaśa Ukthya, a Saptadaśa Ukthya, an Abhyāsaṅgya five-day rite, and a Viśvajit Atirātra.

22.23.13.a.m: One desirous of food [should sacrifice] with the Śalalīpiśaṅga.

22.23.14.a.m: Jyotis, Go, Āyus, Jyotis, Go, Āyus, Āyus, Go, Jyotis, and an Atirātra.

22.23.16.a.s: daśarātrāya dīkṣiṣyamāṇo daśahotāraṃ manasānudrutyāhavanīye sagrahaṃ juhuyāt
22.23.16.a.d: दशरात्राय दीक्षिष्यमाणो दशहोतारं मनसानुद्रुत्याहवनीये सग्रहं जुहुयात्
22.23.16.a.m: Intending to be consecrated for a ten-day rite, having recited the Daśahotṛ mentally, he should offer [it] with the draught into the āhavanīya.

22.23.17.b.m: He becomes pre-eminent among offspring and among his peers.

22.23.18.a.s: trivṛdagniṣṭomaḥ pañcadaśa ukthyastrivṛdagniṣṭomaḥ saptadaśo 'gniṣṭoma ekaviṃśa ukthyaḥ saptadaśo 'gniṣṭomastriṇavo 'gniṣṭomastrayastriṃśa ukthyastriṇavo 'gniṣṭomo viśvajitsarvapṛṣṭho 'tirātraḥ
22.23.18.a.d: त्रिवृदग्निष्टोमः पञ्चदश उक्थ्यस्त्रिवृदग्निष्टोमः सप्तदशो ऽग्निष्टोम एकविंश उक्थ्यः सप्तदशो ऽग्निष्टोमस्त्रिणवो ऽग्निष्टोमस्त्रयस्त्रिंश उक्थ्यस्त्रिणवो ऽग्निष्टोमो विश्वजित्सर्वपृष्ठो ऽतिरात्रः
22.23.18.a.m: A Trivṛt Agniṣṭoma, a Pañcadaśa Ukthya, a Trivṛt Agniṣṭoma, a Saptadaśa Agniṣṭoma, an Ekaviṃśa Ukthya, a Saptadaśa Agniṣṭoma, a Triṇava Agniṣṭoma, a Trayastriṃśa Ukthya, a Triṇava Agniṣṭoma, and a Viśvajit Sarvapṛṣṭha Atirātra.

22.24.1.a.m: One against whom sorcery is being practiced [should sacrifice] with the Devapura.

22.24.2.a.s: triṣṭomo 'gniṣṭomo jyotirukthyastriṣṭomo 'gniṣṭomo 'bhijidagniṣṭomo gaurukthyo 'bhijidagniṣṭomo viśvajidagniṣṭoma āyurukthyo viśvajidagniṣṭomaḥ sarvastomo 'tirātraḥ
22.24.2.a.d: त्रिष्टोमो ऽग्निष्टोमो ज्योतिरुक्थ्यस्त्रिष्टोमो ऽग्निष्टोमो ऽभिजिदग्निष्टोमो गौरुक्थ्यो ऽभिजिदग्निष्टोमो विश्वजिदग्निष्टोम आयुरुक्थ्यो विश्वजिदग्निष्टोमः सर्वस्तोमो ऽतिरात्रः
22.24.2.a.m: A triṣṭoma Agniṣṭoma, a jyotiḥ Ukthya, a triṣṭoma Agniṣṭoma, an abhijit Agniṣṭoma, a go-Ukthya, an abhijit Agniṣṭoma, a viśvajit Agniṣṭoma, an āyur-Ukthya, a viśvajit Agniṣṭoma, and a sarvastoma Atirātra [constitute the rites].

22.24.3.a.m: Through the [rite] accompanied by Chandomas, he obtains man, cattle, vitality, and heroic might.

22.24.4.a.m: [The order is:] an abhyāsaṅgya six-day period, three chandoma days, and an Atirātra.

22.24.5.b.m: An abhyāsaṅgya five-day period, four chandoma days, and an Atirātra.

22.24.6.a.m: By means of the Kausurubinda [rite], one who is already great becomes greater.

22.24.7.a.s: trayastrivṛto 'gniṣṭomāstrayaḥ pañcadaśā ukthyāstrayaḥ saptadaśā ukthyā ekaviṃśo 'tirātraḥ
22.24.7.a.d: त्रयस्त्रिवृतो ऽग्निष्टोमास्त्रयः पञ्चदशा उक्थ्यास्त्रयः सप्तदशा उक्थ्या एकविंशो ऽतिरात्रः
22.24.7.a.m: There are three trivṛt Agniṣṭomas, three fifteenfold Ukthyas, three seventeenfold Ukthyas, and a twenty-one-fold Atirātra.

22.24.8.a.m: The Pauṇḍarīka is an eleven-day rite with a sacrificial gift of ten thousand [cattle].

22.24.9.a.m: Day after day he gives thousands;

22.24.9.b.m: On the last [day], a thousand horses, or a hundred horses.

22.24.10.a.s: tena sarvāmṛddhimṛdhnīti parameṣṭhitāṃ gacchatyabhi svargaṃ lokaṃ jayatyeṣu lokeṣu pratitiṣṭhati
22.24.10.a.d: तेन सर्वामृद्धिमृध्नीति परमेष्ठितां गच्छत्यभि स्वर्गं लोकं जयत्येषु लोकेषु प्रतितिष्ठति
22.24.10.a.m: By this he attains all prosperity, reaches the highest station, conquers the heavenly world, and is established in these worlds.

22.24.11.a.m: An abhyāsaṅgya six-day period, a fourfold Agniṣṭoma, three chandoma days, and an Atirātra.

22.24.12.b.m: An abhyāsaṅgya five-day period, four chandoma days, the Mahāvrata, a Viśvajit with all pṛṣṭhas, and an Atirātra.

22.25.1.a.m: Now, among the unction-sacrifices (sava), the Bṛhaspatisava has been explained.

22.25.3.a.m: He offers the seven oblations beginning with the Agni-oblation.

22.25.4.a.m: A dappled two-year-old heifer dedicated to the Maruts is seized.

22.25.5.a.s: tasyāḥ purastātsviṣṭakṛto yajamānāyatana ṛṣabhacarma prācīnagrīvamuttaralomāstīrya tasminnāsīnaṃ yajamānaṃ dadhnābhiṣiñcati
22.25.5.a.d: तस्याः पुरस्तात्स्विष्टकृतो यजमानायतन ऋषभचर्म प्राचीनग्रीवमुत्तरलोमास्तीर्य तस्मिन्नासीनं यजमानं दध्नाभिषिञ्चति
22.25.5.a.m: Before the sviṣṭakṛt of it, having spread out a bull's hide in the sacrificer's place with its neck pointing eastward and its hairy side upward, he consecrates the sacrificer sitting upon it with sour milk.

22.25.6.a.m: A brāhmaṇa desiring spiritual splendour [performs the following]:

22.25.7.a.m: He offers the eight oblations beginning with the Agni-oblation.

22.25.8.a.s: purastātsviṣṭakṛto hiraṇyena ghṛtamutpūya tena kṛṣṇājina āsīnamabhiṣiñcati
22.25.8.a.d: पुरस्तात्स्विष्टकृतो हिरण्येन घृतमुत्पूय तेन कृष्णाजिन आसीनमभिषिञ्चति
22.25.8.a.m: Before the sviṣṭakṛt, having purified ghee by means of gold, he consecrates him sitting upon a black-antelope skin with it.

22.25.10.a.m: Whatever belongs to the Rājasūya, except for the soma [sacrifice], all that takes place.

22.25.11.a.m: Having concluded the Maitrābārhaspatya [oblation], he seizes a barren cow who has brought forth once, dedicated to Soma.

22.25.12.a.s: tasyāḥ purastātsviṣṭakṛto 'ṣāḍhaṃ yutsu pṛtanāsu paprimiti saumyarcādbhirabhiṣiñcati
22.25.12.a.d: तस्याः पुरस्तात्स्विष्टकृतो ऽषाढं युत्सु पृतनासु पप्रिमिति सौम्यर्चाद्भिरभिषिञ्चति
22.25.12.a.m: Before the sviṣṭakṛt of it, he consecrates him with water with the verse addressed to Soma: 'Unconquered in battles, filling in fights…'

22.25.13.a.s: śeṣaṃ saṃsthāpya saṃsṛpāṃ havirbhirdiśāmaveṣṭyā dvipaśunā paśubandhena sātyadūtānāṃ havirbhiḥ prayujāmiti yajate
22.25.13.a.d: शेषं संस्थाप्य संसृपां हविर्भिर्दिशामवेष्ट्या द्विपशुना पशुबन्धेन सात्यदूतानां हविर्भिः प्रयुजामिति यजते
22.25.13.a.m: Having concluded the remainder, he sacrifices with the oblations of the Saṃsṛps, with the Diśāmaveṣṭi, with the animal sacrifice of two victims, and with the oblations of the Sātyadūtas [known as] the Prayujs.

22.25.14.a.m: One desiring cattle [sacrifices] with the Pṛthisava.

22.25.15.a.m: Whatever belongs to the Rājasūya that does not involve the high altar, all that takes place.

22.25.16.a.s: maitrābārhaspatyasya purastātsviṣṭakṛto ye me pañcāśatamiti nārāśaṃsyarcādbhirabhiṣiñcati
22.25.16.a.d: मैत्राबार्हस्पत्यस्य पुरस्तात्स्विष्टकृतो ये मे पञ्चाशतमिति नाराशंस्यर्चाद्भिरभिषिञ्चति
22.25.16.a.m: Before the sviṣṭakṛt of the Maitrābārhaspatya [oblation], he consecrates him with water with the praise verse of men: 'Those who fifty to me…'

22.25.17.a.m: The subsequent [procedure] is identical with the previous one, with the omission of the animal sacrifice.

22.25.19.a.m: One desiring food [sacrifices] with the Odanasava.

22.25.20.a.m: He sacrifices under the Rohiṇī constellation; he cooks [the mess of rice] at dawn.

22.25.22.a.s: udita āditye siṃhe vyāghra iti catasra āhutīrodanāddhutvā rāḍasi virāḍasītyetaiḥ pratimantram
22.25.22.a.d: उदित आदित्ये सिंहे व्याघ्र इति चतस्र आहुतीरोदनाद्धुत्वा राडसि विराडसीत्येतैः प्रतिमन्त्रम्
22.25.22.a.m: When the sun has risen, having offered four oblations from the mess of rice with the formula 'A lion, a tiger…', [he consecrates him] with these [formulas] verse by verse: 'You are a sovereign; you are an all-ruler…'

22.26.1.b.s: ājyamanthaṃ brāhmaṇaḥ payomanthaṃ rājanyo dadhimanthaṃ vaiśya udamanthaṃ śūdraḥ
22.26.1.b.d: आज्यमन्थं ब्राह्मणः पयोमन्थं राजन्यो दधिमन्थं वैश्य उदमन्थं शूद्रः
22.26.1.b.m: The brāhmaṇa [prepares] a mash with ghee, the rājanya a mash with milk, the vaiśya a mash with sour milk, and the śūdra a mash with water.

22.26.2.a.s: indrāya tvā tejasvate tejasvantaṃ śrīṇāmīti brāhmaṇaḥ saktubhirājyaṃ śrītvā tejo 'sītyabhimantrya tatte prayacchāmīti yajamānāya prayacchati
22.26.2.a.d: इन्द्राय त्वा तेजस्वते तेजस्वन्तं श्रीणामीति ब्राह्मणः सक्तुभिराज्यं श्रीत्वा तेजो ऽसीत्यभिमन्त्र्य तत्ते प्रयच्छामीति यजमानाय प्रयच्छति
22.26.2.a.m: With the formula 'For Indra endowed with splendour, I mix you endowed with splendour', the brāhmaṇa, having mixed the ghee with barley-groats and addressed it with 'You are splendour', hands it to the sacrificer with 'That I offer to you.'

22.26.3.a.m: Having received it with 'Let my mouth be endowed with splendour', he consumes it.

22.26.4.a.d: एवमितरेषामुत्तरौत्तरः श्रयणो ऽभिमन्त्रणः प्रदानो भक्षणश्च यथालिङ्गम्
22.26.4.a.m: In this way for the others, the mixing, addressing, handing over, and consuming are done one after another according to their distinctive marks.

22.26.5.a.m: Having consumed them all, the sacrificer gives gold to the brāhmaṇa;

22.26.5.b.m: A bow with three arrows to the rājanya;

22.26.5.d.m: A leather-bag water-pot to the śūdra.

22.26.6.a.m: The sacrificer eats the remainder of the mess of rice.

22.26.7.a.m: He addresses him while eating with: 'O Agni, make this man [long-lived] for life, for splendour.'

22.26.8.a.m: He fastens gold onto the sacrificer.

22.26.9.a.m: While it is being fastened, he murmurs: 'You are life, you are all-life.'

22.26.10.a.s: apāṃ grahāngṛhṇanti ye manthānkalpayantyapāṃ yo dravaṇe rasa ityetaiḥ pratimantram
22.26.10.a.d: अपां ग्रहान्गृह्णन्ति ये मन्थान्कल्पयन्त्यपां यो द्रवणे रस इत्येतैः प्रतिमन्त्रम्
22.26.10.a.m: Those who prepare the mashes draw draughts of water, each with one of these formulas: 'The juice of the waters which runs in the current…'

22.26.11.a.s: tairenaṃ saṃsṛṣṭairabhiṣiñcati yato vāto manojavā iti
22.26.11.a.d: तैरेनं संसृष्टैरभिषिञ्चति यतो वातो मनोजवा इति
22.26.11.a.m: With them combined, he consecrates him with: 'From where the wind, swift as thought…'

22.26.12.a.m: Having addressed him with 'You are like an ocean, unfathomable', he then purifies him with three clusters of darbha grass.

22.26.13.a.m: 'It serves as a substitute for the final bath,' so it is known.

22.26.14.a.m: In front of the āhavanīya, a chariot stands ready.

22.26.15.a.m: The sacrificer approaches it with: 'Come forward.'

22.26.16.a.m: He addresses him as he mounts it with: 'Mount, O augmenter of friends!'

22.26.17.a.m: With 'The two curved pins, the two lower pins…' he touches the two chariot wheels,

22.26.18.a.m: When he has mounted, [he addresses him] with five [verses beginning with]: 'Mount, O slayer of Vṛtra!'

22.26.19.a.s: didṛkṣeṇyo darśanīyo bhavati ya etena yajata iti vijñāyate
22.26.19.a.d: दिदृक्षेण्यो दर्शनीयो भवति य एतेन यजत इति विज्ञायते
22.26.19.a.m: 'He who sacrifices with this becomes worthy of being seen and handsome,' so it is known.

22.27.5.a.m: "asyājarāso 'gna āyūṃṣi pavase" for the [draught] for Indra and Vāyu.

22.27.5.b.m: The second for the [draught] for Mitra and Varuṇa.

22.27.5.d.m: The fourth and fifth for the Śukra and Manthin [draughts]; the sixth for the Āgrayaṇa [draught].

22.27.6.a.m: He employs another, dedicated to Agni, for the Ukthya [draught].

22.27.8.a.m: He employs [another] for the [draughts] for Indra-and-Agni and for the Viśvedevas.

22.27.9.b.m: "śrudhi śrutkarṇa"—the next is for the Mahendra [draught].

22.27.9.c.m: "viśveṣāmaditiḥ"—[these] three are for the Āditya draught.

22.27.13.a.m: One desirous of power of the senses or desirous of virility should sacrifice with the Indrastut, [which is] an Ukthya with the Indrastoma.

22.27.15.a.m: "tiṣṭhā harī kasya vṛṣā" for the [draught] for Indra and Vāyu.

22.27.15.b.m: The third for the [draught] for Mitra and Varuṇa.

22.27.15.d.m: The fifth and sixth for the Śukra and Manthin [draughts].

22.27.17.a.m: He employs [another] for the Dhruva, Aindrāgna, and Vaiśvadeva [draughts].

22.27.18.a.m: The regular ones are for the Marutvatīya and Mahendra [draughts].

22.27.19.a.m: "ā no viśvābhirūtibhiḥ"—[these] three are for the Āditya draught.

22.27.20.a.m: He employs [another] for the Vaiśvadeva and Pātnīvata [draughts].

22.28.1.a.s: rājābhiṣekṣyamāṇo janapadeṣu samaveteṣu dvayoḥ puṇyāhayoḥ pūrvasminsthaṇḍilaṃ kalpayitvāgnimupasamādhāya saṃparistīrya vasati
22.28.1.a.d: राजाभिषेक्ष्यमाणो जनपदेषु समवेतेषु द्वयोः पुण्याहयोः पूर्वस्मिन्स्थण्डिलं कल्पयित्वाग्निमुपसमाधाय संपरिस्तीर्य वसति
22.28.1.a.m: A king who is to be consecrated, when the people of the realm have assembled, on the earlier of two auspicious days, having prepared a raised mound, having added fuel to the fire, and having strewn [grass] around it, stays [there for the night].

22.28.2.a.s: udita āditye ye keśino narte brahmaṇa iti dve āhutī hutvā rāḍasi virāḍasīti yajamānāyatana audumbarīmāsandīṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati
22.28.2.a.d: उदित आदित्ये ये केशिनो नर्ते ब्रह्मण इति द्वे आहुती हुत्वा राडसि विराडसीति यजमानायतन औदुम्बरीमासन्दीं प्रतिष्ठापयति
22.28.2.a.m: When the sun has risen, having offered two oblations with "ye keśinaḥ" and "narte brahmaṇaḥ", he sets up an udumbara throne in the sacrificer's place with "rāḍasi virāḍasi".

22.28.4.a.m: With "āroha proṣṭham" he addresses him as he mounts.

22.28.6.a.m: Sitting on it, he has his hair shaved with "yenāvapatsavitā kṣureṇa".

22.28.7.a.m: With "mā te keśān" he addresses the hair as it is being scattered.

22.28.8.a.m: Having gathered them together, he places them in a clump of darbha grass with "tebhyo nidhānam".

22.28.9.a.m: Then he anoints him with milk mixed with clarified butter

22.28.9.b.m: his two arms with "balaṃ te bāhuvoh"

22.28.10.a.s: vyāghro 'yamagnāviti saptāhutīrhutvā dyaurasi pṛthivyasīti yajamānāyatane śārdūlacarma prācīnagrīvamuttaralomāstṛṇāti
22.28.10.a.d: व्याघ्रो ऽयमग्नाविति सप्ताहुतीर्हुत्वा द्यौरसि पृथिव्यसीति यजमानायतने शार्दूलचर्म प्राचीनग्रीवमुत्तरलोमास्तृणाति
22.28.10.a.m: Having offered seven oblations with "vyāghro 'yamagnau", he spreads a tiger skin with the neck to the east and the hair side up in the sacrificer's place with "dyaurasi pṛthivyasi".

22.28.12.a.m: With "vyāghro vaiyyāghraḥ" he addresses him as he sits.

22.28.13.a.s: athainaṃ tokmāvāstābhirdūrvāvāstābhirvādbhirabhiṣiñcati yā divyā āpa iti pratipadyā pāṅktāt
22.28.13.a.d: अथैनं तोक्मावास्ताभिर्दूर्वावास्ताभिर्वाद्भिरभिषिञ्चति या दिव्या आप इति प्रतिपद्या पाङ्क्तात्
22.28.13.a.m: Then he sprinkles him with water containing green barley sprouts or water containing dūrvā grass, beginning with "yā divyā āpaḥ" down to the end of the pāṅkta verse.

22.28.14.a.s: aruṇaṃ tvā vṛkamityenamabhimantrya pra bāhaveti bāhū prasāryendrasya te vīryakṛta ityupāvaharati
22.28.14.a.d: अरुणं त्वा वृकमित्येनमभिमन्त्र्य प्र बाहवेति बाहू प्रसार्येन्द्रस्य ते वीर्यकृत इत्युपावहरति
22.28.14.a.m: Having addressed him with "aruṇaṃ tvā vṛkam", having extended his two arms with "pra bāhava", he brings them down with "indrasya te vīryakṛte".

22.28.15.a.m: A chariot stands placed in front of the fire.

22.28.16.a.m: The king goes towards it with "abhi prehī".

22.28.17.a.m: With "ātiṣṭha vṛtrahantama" he addresses him as he mounts.

22.28.18.a.m: With "aṅkau nyaṅkau" he touches the two chariot wheels

22.28.19.a.m: With "namasta ṛṣe" he addresses the royal chaplain.

22.28.21.a.m: With "ā raśmīn" he takes hold of the reins.

22.28.22.a.m: With the six [verses] beginning with "ātiṣṭha vṛtrahan" [he addresses him] when he has mounted.

22.28.23.a.m: Having made him recite the two [verses] beginning with "pari mā senyāḥ" and having addressed him with the next three, he makes him look up at the sun with "udasāvetu".

22.28.24.a.m: With "annavatām" he surveys the people of the realm.

22.28.27.a.m: The savas are concluded; the savas [are concluded].

23.1.1.a.m: Up to twenty-four [persons] may sit [for] a sattra.

23.1.2.a.s: teṣāṃ dvādaśāhena sattrabhūtena kalpo vyākhyāto yāni purastātsaṃvatsarāt /
23.1.2.a.d: तेषां द्वादशाहेन सत्त्रभूतेन कल्पो व्याख्यातो यानि पुरस्तात्संवत्सरात् ।
23.1.2.a.m: For those [sattras] which are before [i.e. shorter than] a year, the procedure is explained by the Dvādaśāha in its form as a sattra;

23.1.3.a.m: There are Atirātras on both ends [of them],

23.1.4.a.s: tṛtīyaṃ pañcadaśarātraṃ parihāpya kuṇḍapāyināṃ ca sattram
23.1.4.a.d: तृतीयं पञ्चदशरात्रं परिहाप्य कुण्डपायिनां च सत्त्रम्
23.1.4.a.m: with the exception of the third fifteen-day rite (Pañcadaśarātra) and the sattra of the Kuṇḍapāyins.

23.1.5.a.s: ṛtūnāmekādaśarātreṇa prajāṃ sṛjante prajāmavarundhate prajāṃ vindante prajāvanto bhavanti
23.1.5.a.d: ऋतूनामेकादशरात्रेण प्रजां सृजन्ते प्रजामवरुन्धते प्रजां विन्दन्ते प्रजावन्तो भवन्ति
23.1.5.a.m: By means of the eleven-day rite (Ekādaśarātra) of the seasons, they generate offspring, secure offspring, obtain offspring, and become possessors of offspring.

23.1.6.a.m: [Its order is:] an Atirātra, a Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, three Chandomas, [and] an Atirātra.

23.1.8.a.m: Whatever desire they desire, that they obtain.

23.1.9.a.d: अतिरात्रः पृष्ठ्यः षडहः सर्वस्तोमो ऽतिरात्रश्चत्वारश्छन्दोमा अतिरात्रः
23.1.9.a.m: [The first has:] an Atirātra, a Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, a Sarvastoma Atirātra, four Chandomas, [and] an Atirātra.

23.1.10.a.m: Those desirous of spiritual lustre should undertake the second.

23.1.11.a.m: [Its order is:] an Atirātra, the ten days of the Dvādaśāha, the Mahāvrata, and an Atirātra.

23.1.13.a.m: Whatever desire they desire, that they obtain.

23.1.14.a.s: atirātraḥ pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍaha āvṛttaḥ pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍaho 'tirātraḥ
23.1.14.a.d: अतिरात्रः पृष्ठ्यः षडह आवृत्तः पृष्ठ्यः षडहो ऽतिरात्रः
23.1.14.a.m: [The first has:] an Atirātra, a Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, a reversed Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, [and] an Atirātra.

23.1.15.a.s: dvitīyaṃ yāṃstalpa udake vivāhe vā mīmāṃseran
23.1.15.a.d: द्वितीयं यांस्तल्प उदके विवाहे वा मीमांसेरन्
23.1.15.a.m: Those regarding whom people might question regarding bed, water, or marriage should undertake the second.

23.1.16.a.m: [Its order is:] two Atirātras, a three-day rite of Jyotis, Gauḥ, and Āyus, a Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, Āyus, Gauḥ, Jyotis, [and] an Atirātra.

23.1.17.a.m: Those desirous of prosperity should undertake the third.

23.1.18.a.m: [Its order is:] an Atirātra, the Gauḥ and Āyus [days], the ten days of the Dvādaśāha, [and] an Atirātra.

23.2.3.a.m: On the new moon is the opening day (prāyaṇīya); on the eighth day is the Mahāvrata; on the full moon is the concluding day (udayanīya);

23.2.4.a.s: atirātraḥ pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍaho mahāvratamāvṛttaḥ pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍaho 'tirātraḥ
23.2.4.a.d: अतिरात्रः पृष्ठ्यः षडहो महाव्रतमावृत्तः पृष्ठ्यः षडहो ऽतिरात्रः
23.2.4.a.m: [The first has:] an Atirātra, a Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, the Mahāvrata, a reversed Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, [and] an Atirātra.

23.2.5.a.m: Those desirous of spiritual lustre should undertake the second.

23.2.6.a.m: [Its order is:] an Atirātra, the Trivṛt-Agniṣṭut, a three-day rite of Jyotis, Gauḥ, and Āyus, a Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, Āyus, Gauḥ, Jyotis, [and] an Atirātra.

23.2.7.a.m: By means of the third they secure both desires: that which is in a sattra and that which is in an ahīna.

23.2.8.a.m: [Its order is:] the Trivṛt-Agniṣṭut, a three-day rite of Jyotis, Gauḥ, and Āyus, the ten days of the Dvādaśāha, [and] an Atirātra.

23.2.9.a.m: By means of the fourth they propagate indeed with offspring and cattle.

23.2.10.a.m: [Its order is:] an Atirātra, a three-day rite of Jyotis, Gauḥ, and Āyus, the ten days of the Dvādaśāha, [and] an Atirātra.

23.2.11.a.m: Those desirous of vigor should undertake the sixteen-day rite (Ṣoḍaśarātra) dedicated to Indra.

23.2.13.a.m: Those desirous of food should undertake the seventeen-day rite (Saptadaśarātra).

23.2.14.a.m: [Its order is:] an Atirātra, a five-day rite of Jyotis, Gauḥ, Āyus, Gauḥ, and Āyus, the ten days of the Dvādaśāha, [and] an Atirātra.

23.2.15.a.m: Those desirous of cattle should undertake the eighteen-day rite (Aṣṭādaśarātra).

23.2.16.a.m: [Its order is:] an Atirātra, an Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha, the ten days of the Dvādaśāha, [and] an Atirātra.

23.2.17.a.m: By means of the nineteen-day rite (Ekānnaviṃśatirātra) they propagate with offspring and cattle.

23.2.19.a.m: By means of the twenty-day rite (Viṃśatirātra) they become endowed with spiritual lustre and eaters of food.

23.2.20.a.d: अतिरात्रो ऽभिप्लवः षडहो ऽभिजिद्विश्वजितौ द्वादशाहस्य दशाहान्यतिरात्रः
23.2.20.a.m: [Its order is:] an Atirātra, an Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha, the Abhijit and Viśvajit, the ten days of the Dvādaśāha, [and] an Atirātra.

23.3.2.a.m: Whatever desire they desire, that they obtain.

23.3.3.a.m: [The first has:] an Atirātra, an Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha, an Atirātra, two Abhiplavas, [and] an Atirātra.

23.3.4.a.m: Those desirous of spiritual lustre should undertake the second.

23.3.5.a.m: A victim dedicated to Soma and Pūṣan is to be seized.

23.3.6.a.m: The verses of Manu are the kindling verses (sāmidhenīs).

23.3.9.a.s: atirātraḥ pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍahastrayaḥ svarasāmāno divākīrtyamahastrayaḥ svarasāmāna āvṛttaḥ pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍaho 'tirātraḥ
23.3.9.a.d: अतिरात्रः पृष्ठ्यः षडहस्त्रयः स्वरसामानो दिवाकीर्त्यमहस्त्रयः स्वरसामान आवृत्तः पृष्ठ्यः षडहो ऽतिरात्रः
23.3.9.a.m: [Its order is:] an Atirātra, a Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, three Svarasāmans, the Divākīrtya day, three Svarasāmans, a reversed Pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha, [and] an Atirātra.

23.3.10.a.m: By means of the twenty-two-day rite (Dvāviṃśatirātra) they secure food from the year, from these worlds, and from that sun.

23.3.11.a.s: atirātro jyotirgaurāyustryaho 'bhiplavaḥ ṣaḍaho dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni mahāvratamatirātraśca
23.3.11.a.d: अतिरात्रो ज्योतिर्गौरायुस्त्र्यहो ऽभिप्लवः षडहो द्वादशाहस्य दशाहानि महाव्रतमतिरात्रश्च
23.3.11.a.m: [Its order is:] an Atirātra, a three-day rite of Jyotis, Gauḥ, and Āyus, an Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha, the ten days of the Dvādaśāha, the Mahāvrata, and an Atirātra.

23.3.12.a.m: Those desirous of cattle should undertake the twenty-three-day rite (Trayoviṃśatirātra).

23.3.13.a.d: अतिरात्रो ज्योतिर्गौरायुर्गौरायुःपञ्चाहो ऽभिप्लवः षडहो द्वादशाहस्य दशाहान्यतिरात्रः
23.3.13.a.m: [Its order is:] an Atirātra, a five-day rite of Jyotis, Gauḥ, Āyus, Gauḥ, and Āyus, an Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha, the ten days of the Dvādaśāha, [and] an Atirātra.

23.3.15.a.m: Whatever desire they desire, that they obtain.

23.3.16.a.m: [The first has:] an Atirātra, two Abhiplavas, the ten days of the Dvādaśāha, [and] an Atirātra.

23.4.1.a.m: By means of the twenty-four-day rite known as the Saṃsad they sit in the heavenly world.

23.4.2.a.s: atirātraścaturviṃśa ukthya ārambhaṇīyastrivṛdvā pṛṣṭhyastomaḥ ṣaḍahastrayastriṃśamaharaniruktaṃ trayastriṃśaṃ niruktaṃ triṇavaṃ dve ekaviṃśe triṇavaṃ trayastriṃśamaharniruktaṃ trayastriṃśamaniruktaṃ pṛṣṭhyastomaḥ ṣaḍahaḥ pratyaṅ trivṛdaharaniruktmā jyotiṣṭomo vaiśvānaro 'tirātraḥ
23.4.2.a.d: अतिरात्रश्चतुर्विंश उक्थ्य आरम्भणीयस्त्रिवृद्वा पृष्ठ्यस्तोमः षडहस्त्रयस्त्रिंशमहरनिरुक्तं त्रयस्त्रिंशं निरुक्तं त्रिणवं द्वे एकविंशे त्रिणवं त्रयस्त्रिंशमहर्निरुक्तं त्रयस्त्रिंशमनिरुक्तं पृष्ठ्यस्तोमः षडहः प्रत्यङ् त्रिवृदहरनिरुक्त्मा ज्योतिष्टोमो वैश्वानरो ऽतिरात्रः
23.4.2.a.m: [Its order is:] an Atirātra, an introductory Ukthya day of twenty-four parts, or [a Trivṛt day], a Pṛṣṭhya-stoma ṣaḍaha, an unexpressed thirty-three-part day, an expressed thirty-three-part day, a twenty-seven-part [day], two twenty-one-part [days], a twenty-seven-part [day], an expressed thirty-three-part day, an unexpressed thirty-three-part day, a Pṛṣṭhya-stoma ṣaḍaha, an unexpressed reverse Trivṛt day, a Jyotiṣṭoma, a Vaiśvānara [day], [and] an Atirātra.

23.4.3.a.m: Those desirous of cattle should undertake the twenty-five-day rite (Pañcaviṃśatirātra).

23.4.4.a.m: [The twenty-five-night rite consists of:] an Atirātra, two Abhiplavas, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, the Mahāvrata, and an Atirātra.

23.4.5.a.m: Those desiring heaven should undertake the twenty-six-night rite.

23.4.6.a.m: [It consists of:] an Atirātra, the Go and Āyus days, two Abhiplavas, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, [and] an Atirātra.

23.4.7.a.m: Those desiring proper food should undertake the twenty-seven-night rite.

23.4.8.a.m: [It consists of:] an Atirātra, the three-day rite of Jyotis, Go, and Āyus, two Abhiplavas, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, [and] an Atirātra.

23.4.9.a.m: Those desiring cattle should undertake the twenty-eight-night rite.

23.4.11.a.m: By means of the twenty-nine-night rite, they win boundless prosperity.

23.4.12.a.m: [It consists of:] an Atirātra, the five-day rite of Jyotis, Go, Āyus, Go, and Āyus, two Abhiplavas, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, [and] an Atirātra.

23.4.13.a.m: Those desiring proper food should undertake the thirty-night rite.

23.4.14.a.m: [It consists of:] an Atirātra, three Abhiplavas, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, [and] an Atirātra.

23.5.1.a.m: Those desiring proper food should undertake the thirty-one-night rite.

23.5.3.a.m: Those desiring firm standing should undertake the thirty-two-night rite.

23.5.4.a.d: अतिरात्रो गोआयुषी त्रयो ऽभिप्लवा द्वादशाहस्य दशाहान्यतिरात्रः
23.5.4.a.m: [It consists of:] an Atirātra, the Go and Āyus days, three Abhiplavas, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, [and] an Atirātra.

23.5.6.a.m: Whatever desire they desire, that they obtain.

23.5.7.a.s: atirātrastrayaḥ pañcāhā viśvajidatirātra ekaḥ pañcāho dvādaśāhasya daśāhānyatirātraḥ
23.5.7.a.d: अतिरात्रस्त्रयः पञ्चाहा विश्वजिदतिरात्र एकः पञ्चाहो द्वादशाहस्य दशाहान्यतिरात्रः
23.5.7.a.m: [The first consists of:] an Atirātra, three five-day rites, a Viśvajit Atirātra, one five-day rite, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, [and] an Atirātra.

23.5.8.a.m: Those desiring spiritual splendor should undertake the second [thirty-three-night rite].

23.5.9.a.s: atirātro 'bhiplavaḥ ṣaḍaho 'tirātro 'bhiplavaḥ ṣaḍaho 'tirātre 'bhiplavaḥ ṣaḍaho dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni mahāvratamatirātraśca
23.5.9.a.d: अतिरात्रो ऽभिप्लवः षडहो ऽतिरात्रो ऽभिप्लवः षडहो ऽतिरात्रे ऽभिप्लवः षडहो द्वादशाहस्य दशाहानि महाव्रतमतिरात्रश्च
23.5.9.a.m: [It consists of:] an Atirātra, an Abhiplava six-day rite, an Atirātra, an Abhiplava six-day rite, an Atirātra, an Abhiplava six-day rite, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, the Mahāvrata, and an Atirātra.

23.5.10.a.m: Those desiring prosperity should undertake the third [thirty-three-night rite].

23.5.11.a.m: [It consists of:] an Atirātra, three five-day rites, an Atirātra, three five-day rites, [and] an Atirātra.

23.5.12.a.m: Those desiring bodily vigor should undertake the thirty-four-night rite.

23.5.13.a.d: अतिरात्रो ज्योतिर्गौरायुस्त्र्यहस्त्रयो ऽभिप्लवा द्वादशाहस्य दशाहानि महाव्रतमतिरात्रश्च
23.5.13.a.m: [It consists of:] an Atirātra, the three-day rite of Jyotis, Go, and Āyus, three Abhiplavas, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, the Mahāvrata, and an Atirātra.

23.6.1.a.m: Those desiring cattle should undertake the thirty-five-night rite.

23.6.2.a.m: [It consists of:] an Atirātra, the five-day rite of Jyotis, Go, Āyus, Go, and Āyus, three Abhiplavas, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, [and] an Atirātra.

23.6.3.a.m: Those desiring heaven should undertake the thirty-six-night rite.

23.6.4.a.m: [It consists of:] an Atirātra, four Abhiplavas, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, [and] an Atirātra.

23.6.5.a.m: Those desiring proper food should undertake the thirty-seven-night rite.

23.6.7.a.m: Those desiring cattle should undertake the thirty-eight-night rite.

23.6.8.a.d: अतिरात्रो गोआयुषी चत्वारो ऽभिप्लवा द्वादशाहस्य दशाहान्यतिरात्रः
23.6.8.a.m: [It consists of:] an Atirātra, the Go and Āyus days, four Abhiplavas, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, [and] an Atirātra.

23.6.9.a.m: By means of the thirty-nine-night rite, they win endless prosperity.

23.6.10.a.m: [It consists of:] an Atirātra, the three-day rite of Jyotis, Go, and Āyus, four Abhiplavas, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, [and] an Atirātra.

23.6.11.a.m: By means of the forty-night rite, they firmly establish themselves in the supreme Virāj.

23.7.1.a.m: There are seven forty-nine-night rites [called] the Vidhṛtis.

23.7.2.a.m: By the first, they turn away evil [and] the rival.

23.7.3.a.s: atirātrastrayastrivṛto 'gnīṣṭomā atirātro daśa pañcadaśā ukthyāḥ ṣoḍaśimaddaśamamaharatirātro dvādaśa saptadaśā ukthyā atirātraḥ pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍaho 'tirātro dvādaśaikaviṃśā ukthyā atirātraḥ
23.7.3.a.d: अतिरात्रस्त्रयस्त्रिवृतो ऽग्नीष्टोमा अतिरात्रो दश पञ्चदशा उक्थ्याः षोडशिमद्दशममहरतिरात्रो द्वादश सप्तदशा उक्थ्या अतिरात्रः पृष्ठ्यः षडहो ऽतिरात्रो द्वादशैकविंशा उक्थ्या अतिरात्रः
23.7.3.a.m: [It consists of:] an Atirātra, three trivṛt Agniṣṭomas, an Atirātra, ten fifteen-verse Ukthyas with the tenth day having the Ṣoḍaśin, an Atirātra, twelve seventeen-verse Ukthyas, an Atirātra, a Pṛṣṭhya six-day rite, an Atirātra, twelve twenty-one-verse Ukthyas, [and] an Atirātra.

23.7.5.a.s: yamevaiṣāṃ śrīrbhavati mitraśca varuṇaśca dhātā cāryamā cāṃśaśca bhagaścendraśca vivasvāṃścaitāsāṃ devatānāmṛddhimṛdhnuvanti
23.7.5.a.d: यमेवैषां श्रीर्भवति मित्रश्च वरुणश्च धाता चार्यमा चांशश्च भगश्चेन्द्रश्च विवस्वांश्चैतासां देवतानामृद्धिमृध्नुवन्ति
23.7.5.a.m: Restrained indeed is their prosperity; Mitra, Varuṇa, Dhātṛ, Aryaman, Aṃśa, Bhaga, Indra, and Vivasvat—they prosper with the prosperity of these deities.

23.7.6.a.s: atirātro dvāvabhiplavau goāyuṣī dvāvabhiplavāvabhijidviśvajiccātirātrāveko 'bhiplavaḥ sarvastomo navasapatadaśaścātirātrau dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni mahāvratamatirātraśca
23.7.6.a.d: अतिरात्रो द्वावभिप्लवौ गोआयुषी द्वावभिप्लवावभिजिद्विश्वजिच्चातिरात्रावेको ऽभिप्लवः सर्वस्तोमो नवसपतदशश्चातिरात्रौ द्वादशाहस्य दशाहानि महाव्रतमतिरात्रश्च
23.7.6.a.m: [It consists of:] an Atirātra, two Abhiplavas, the Go and Āyus days, two Abhiplavas, the Abhijit and Viśvajit as Atirātras, one Abhiplava, the Sarvastoma and the seventeen-day rite as Atirātras, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, the Mahāvrata, and an Atirātra.

23.7.8.a.d: यान्न जानीयुर्यदा चाञ्जते ऽभि चाञ्जते जानान्त्येनाम् ।
23.7.8.a.m: [Those] whom they might not know, when they salve and anoint themselves, they know them.

23.7.9.a.s: gaulgulavena prātaḥsavane saugandhikena mādhyaṃdine pautudraveṇa tṛtīyasavane
23.7.9.a.d: गौल्गुलवेन प्रातःसवने सौगन्धिकेन माध्यंदिने पौतुद्रवेण तृतीयसवने
23.7.9.a.m: [They salve and anoint] with bdellium ointment at the morning pressing, with sweet-scented ointment at the midday pressing, and with deodar ointment at the third pressing.

23.7.10.a.d: अतिरात्रश्चत्वारो ऽभिप्लवाः सर्वस्तोमो ऽतिरात्रो द्वावभिप्लवौ द्वादशाहस्य दशाहान्यतिरात्रः
23.7.10.a.m: [It consists of:] an Atirātra, four Abhiplavas, a Sarvastoma Atirātra, two Abhiplavas, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, [and] an Atirātra.

23.7.12.a.m: They prosper with the prosperity of the year.

23.7.13.a.s: atirātraścaturviṃśa ukthya ārambhaṇīyastrivṛdvā trayo 'bhiplavā abhijittrayaḥ svarasāmāno divākīrtyamahastrayaḥ svarasāmāno viśvajideko 'bhiplava āvṛtta āyurgaurdvādaśāhasya daśāhāni mahāvratamatirātraśca
23.7.13.a.d: अतिरात्रश्चतुर्विंश उक्थ्य आरम्भणीयस्त्रिवृद्वा त्रयो ऽभिप्लवा अभिजित्त्रयः स्वरसामानो दिवाकीर्त्यमहस्त्रयः स्वरसामानो विश्वजिदेको ऽभिप्लव आवृत्त आयुर्गौर्द्वादशाहस्य दशाहानि महाव्रतमतिरात्रश्च
23.7.13.a.m: [It consists of:] an Atirātra, a twenty-four-verse Ukthya introductory day or a trivṛt day, three Abhiplavas, the Abhijit, three Svarasāman days, the Divākīrtya day, three Svarasāman days, the Viśvajit, one reversed Abhiplava, the Āyus and Go days, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, the Mahāvrata, and an Atirātra.

23.8.1.a.m: The fifth is the Savituḥ Kakubhaḥ.

23.8.2.a.m: They attain the instigation of all proper food.

23.8.3.a.s: atirātro nava trivṛntyahānyagniṣṭomamukhaḥ ṣaḍaho 'tha yāti trīṇyagniṣṭomāvabhita ukthyaṃ madhye tathaiva nava pañcadaśāni tathaiva nava saptadaśāni tatahiva navaikaviṃśāni dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni mahāvratamatirātraśca
23.8.3.a.d: अतिरात्रो नव त्रिवृन्त्यहान्यग्निष्टोममुखः षडहो ऽथ याति त्रीण्यग्निष्टोमावभित उक्थ्यं मध्ये तथैव नव पञ्चदशानि तथैव नव सप्तदशानि ततहिव नवैकविंशानि द्वादशाहस्य दशाहानि महाव्रतमतिरात्रश्च
23.8.3.a.m: [It consists of:] an Atirātra, nine trivṛt days: a six-day rite beginning with an Agniṣṭoma, then it proceeds with three days having Agniṣṭomas on both sides and an Ukthya in the middle; likewise nine fifteen-verse days, likewise nine seventeen-verse days, likewise nine twenty-one-verse days, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, the Mahāvrata, and an Atirātra.

23.8.4.a.m: Those desiring firm standing should undertake the sixth.

23.8.5.a.d: अतिरात्रश्चत्वारो ऽभिप्लवा महाव्रतं द्वावभिप्लवौ द्वादशाहस्य दशाहान्यतिरात्रः
23.8.5.a.m: [It consists of:] an Atirātra, four Abhiplavas, the Mahāvrata, two Abhiplavas, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, [and] an Atirātra.

23.8.6.a.m: By the seventh, they surpass other creatures [and] become most vigorous.

23.8.7.a.m: [It consists of:] an Atirātra, six Abhiplavas, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, the Mahāvrata, and an Atirātra.

23.8.8.a.m: Those desiring prosperity should undertake the sixty-one-night rite.

23.8.9.a.s: deva varuṇa devayajanaṃ me dehīti devayajanamadhyavasāya juhoti
23.8.9.a.d: देव वरुण देवयजनं मे देहीति देवयजनमध्यवसाय जुहोति
23.8.9.a.m: Having decided upon the place of sacrificial worship with the formula, 'O divine Varuṇa, grant me the place of sacrificial worship,' he offers an oblation.

23.8.10.a.s: atirātraścaturviṃśa ukthya ārambhaṇīyastrivṛdvā pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍahastrayo 'bhiplavā abhijittrayaḥ svarasāmāno divākīrtyamahastrayaḥ svarasāmāno viśvajidāvṛttaḥ pṛṣṭhyaḥ ṣaḍaha eko 'bhiplava āvṛtta āyurgaurdvādaśāhasya daśāhāni mahāvratamatirātraśca
23.8.10.a.d: अतिरात्रश्चतुर्विंश उक्थ्य आरम्भणीयस्त्रिवृद्वा पृष्ठ्यः षडहस्त्रयो ऽभिप्लवा अभिजित्त्रयः स्वरसामानो दिवाकीर्त्यमहस्त्रयः स्वरसामानो विश्वजिदावृत्तः पृष्ठ्यः षडह एको ऽभिप्लव आवृत्त आयुर्गौर्द्वादशाहस्य दशाहानि महाव्रतमतिरात्रश्च
23.8.10.a.m: [It consists of:] an Atirātra, a twenty-four-verse Ukthya introductory day or a trivṛt day, a Pṛṣṭhya six-day rite, three Abhiplavas, the Abhijit, three Svarasāman days, the Divākīrtya day, three Svarasāman days, the Viśvajit, a reversed Pṛṣṭhya six-day rite, one reversed Abhiplava, the Āyus and Go days, the ten days of the twelve-day rite, the Mahāvrata, and an Atirātra.

23.8.11.a.m: By means of the Hundred-night sacrifice of the gods they attain full life and become wealthier.

23.8.12.a.m: An atirātra, the Jyotis-Gauḥ-Āyus three-day period, fourteen abhiplavas, the ten days of the twelve-day sacrifice, the Mahāvrata, and an atirātra.

23.8.13.a.m: They press [the soma] moving forward, or at the same place.

23.9.1.a.s: ādityānāmayanena prajātiṃ bhūmānaṃ gacchantyabhi svargaṃ lokaṃ jayantyeṣu lokeṣu pratitiṣṭhanti
23.9.1.a.d: आदित्यानामयनेन प्रजातिं भूमानं गच्छन्त्यभि स्वर्गं लोकं जयन्त्येषु लोकेषु प्रतितिष्ठन्ति
23.9.1.a.m: By means of the Course of the Ādityas they attain offspring and abundance, conquer heaven, and establish themselves in these worlds.

23.9.2.a.m: It is explained by the Course of the Cows.

23.9.4.a.m: The months are trivṛt and pañcadaśa, with the pṛṣṭhya in the middle.

23.9.5.a.m: In place of the abhijit is the trivṛt Bṛhaspatisava;

23.9.5.b.m: in place of the viśvajit is the pañcadaśa ukthya Indrastoma.

23.9.6.a.s: tasmādanantaraṃ pṛṣṭhyābhiplavāvupetya dvādaśāhīyasya daśarātrasya vyūḍhā agniṣṭomāstrivṛtaḥ
23.9.6.a.d: तस्मादनन्तरं पृष्ठ्याभिप्लवावुपेत्य द्वादशाहीयस्य दशरात्रस्य व्यूढा अग्निष्टोमास्त्रिवृतः
23.9.6.a.m: Next after it, having undertaken a pṛṣṭhya and an abhiplava, of the ten-day period belonging to the twelve-day sacrifice, the agniṣṭomas are rearranged as trivṛt.

23.9.7.a.m: With the udbhid and valabhid, thus the month deficient by two days is completed.

23.9.8.a.s: āyuṣaṃ gāṃ copetya chandomadaśarātraḥ pratyaṅṅaṣṭācatvāriṃśaṃ catuścatvāriṃśaṃ catvāriṃśaṃ ṣaṭtriṃśaṃ dvātriṃśaṃ triṃśaṃ dve aṣṭāviṃśe pañcaviṃśaṃ caturviṃśam
23.9.8.a.d: आयुषं गां चोपेत्य छन्दोमदशरात्रः प्रत्यङ्ङष्टाचत्वारिंशं चतुश्चत्वारिंशं चत्वारिंशं षट्त्रिंशं द्वात्रिंशं त्रिंशं द्वे अष्टाविंशे पञ्चविंशं चतुर्विंशम्
23.9.8.a.m: And having undertaken the āyus and gauḥ, the Chandoma ten-day period is in reverse order: a forty-eight-versed, a forty-four-versed, a forty-versed, a thirty-six-versed, a thirty-two-versed, a thirty-versed, two twenty-eight-versed, a twenty-five-versed, and a twenty-four-versed.

23.9.9.a.m: With the Mahāvrata and the concluding [atirātra], thus the month deficient by two days is completed.

23.9.10.a.m: By this, the Course of the Aṅgirases is explained.

23.9.13.a.m: The months have the pṛṣṭhyas before, prior to the viṣuvant;

23.9.13.b.m: above the viṣuvant, they have the pṛṣṭhyas after, being pañcadaśa.

23.9.14.a.s: chandomadaśarātra ūrdhvastomaścaturviṃśaṃ pañcaviṃśaṃ dve aṣṭāviṃśe triṃśaṃ dvātriṃśaṃ ṣaṭtriṃśaṃ catvāriṃśaṃ catuścatvāriṃśamaṣṭācatvāriṃśam
23.9.14.a.d: छन्दोमदशरात्र ऊर्ध्वस्तोमश्चतुर्विंशं पञ्चविंशं द्वे अष्टाविंशे त्रिंशं द्वात्रिंशं षट्त्रिंशं चत्वारिंशं चतुश्चत्वारिंशमष्टाचत्वारिंशम्
23.9.14.a.m: The Chandoma ten-day period is in ascending order of stomas: a twenty-four-versed, a twenty-five-versed, two twenty-eight-versed, a thirty-versed, a thirty-two-versed, a thirty-six-versed, a forty-versed, a forty-four-versed, and a forty-eight-versed.

23.9.15.a.m: With the Mahāvrata and the concluding [atirātra], thus the month deficient by two days is completed.

23.9.16.b.m: the pṛṣṭhyas and the ākṣyantis are the Course of the Ādityas, and the abhiplavas and the ākṣyantis are the Course of the Aṅgirases;

23.9.16.c.m: whatever is other than the pṛṣṭhyas and abhiplavas, they call those ākṣyantis.

23.10.1.a.m: By means of the Course of Dṛti and Vātavant they attain whatever desire they desire.

23.10.3.a.s: trivṛtā māsaṃ pñcadaśena māsaṃ saptadaśena māsamekaviṃśena māsaṃ triṇavena māsaṃ trayastriṃśena māsam
23.10.3.a.d: त्रिवृता मासं प्ञ्चदशेन मासं सप्तदशेन मासमेकविंशेन मासं त्रिणवेन मासं त्रयस्त्रिंशेन मासम्
23.10.3.a.m: A month with trivṛt, a month with pañcadaśa, a month with saptadaśa, a month with ekaviṃśa, a month with triṇava, a month with trayastriṃśa;

23.10.4.a.m: then the viṣuvant or the Mahāvrata;

23.10.5.a.m: these very same later months begin with trayastriṃśa and end with trivṛt.

23.10.6.a.m: In the Course of the Kuṇḍapāyins they remain consecrated for a month.

23.10.7.a.m: Having performed the introductory offering and purchased the king [Soma], they tie it up and lay it down.

23.10.8.a.m: Having performed twelve upasads, they sacrifice with the haviryajñas.

23.10.9.a.m: For a month they offer the agnihotra;

23.10.9.b.s: māsaṃ darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ yajante māsaṃ vaiśvadevena māsaṃ varuṇapraghāsairmāsaṃ sākamedhairmāsaṃ śunāsīrīyeṇa //
23.10.9.b.d: मासं दर्शपूर्णमासाभ्यां यजन्ते मासं वैश्वदेवेन मासं वरुणप्रघासैर्मासं साकमेधैर्मासं शुनासीरीयेण ॥
23.10.9.b.m: for a month they sacrifice with the New and Full Moon sacrifices, for a month with the Vaiśvadeva, for a month with the Varuṇapraghāsas, for a month with the Sākamedhas, and for a month with the Śunāsīrīya.

23.10.9.c.s: trivṛtā māsaṃ pañcadaśena māsaṃ saptadaśena māsamekaviṃśena māsaṃ triṇavena māsam /
23.10.9.c.d: त्रिवृता मासं पञ्चदशेन मासं सप्तदशेन मासमेकविंशेन मासं त्रिणवेन मासम् ।
23.10.9.c.m: For a month with trivṛt, for a month with pañcadaśa, for a month with saptadaśa, for a month with ekaviṃśa, for a month with triṇava;

23.10.9.d.s: aṣṭādaśa trayastriṃśānyahāni dvādaśāhasya daśāhāni mahāvratamatirātraśceti dvādaśa māsāḥ
23.10.9.d.d: अष्टादश त्रयस्त्रिंशान्यहानि द्वादशाहस्य दशाहानि महाव्रतमतिरात्रश्चेति द्वादश मासाः
23.10.9.d.m: eighteen trayastriṃśa days, the ten days of the twelve-day sacrifice, the Mahāvrata, and an atirātra—thus are the twelve months.

23.10.10.a.m: They become everything; they prosper with every prosperity.
