23.10.11.a.m: They partake [of soma] with handleless goblets.

23.10.12.a.d: यो होता सो ऽध्वर्युः स पोता ।
23.10.12.a.m: He who is the hotṛ is the adhvaryu and the potṛ;

23.10.12.b.d: य उद्गाता स नेष्टा सो ऽच्छावाकः ।
23.10.12.b.m: he who is the udgātṛ is the neṣṭṛ and the acchāvāka;

23.10.12.c.s: yo maitrāvaruṇaḥ sa brahmā sa pratihartā /
23.10.12.c.d: यो मैत्रावरुणः स ब्रह्मा स प्रतिहर्ता ।
23.10.12.c.m: he who is the maitrāvaruṇa is the brahman and the pratihartṛ;

23.10.12.d.s: yaḥ prastotā sa brāhmaṇācchaṃsī sa grāvastut /
23.10.12.d.d: यः प्रस्तोता स ब्राह्मणाच्छंसी स ग्रावस्तुत् ।
23.10.12.d.m: he who is the prastotṛ is the brāhmaṇācchaṃsin and the grāvastut;

23.10.12.e.m: he who is the pratiprasthātṛ is the agnīdh and the unnetṛ;

23.11.1.a.m: Those desiring heaven should undertake the Course of the Tapaścits.

23.11.3.a.m: He offers [libations] for four months each with one upasad mantra.

23.11.4.a.m: Following each upasad he piles the fire altar.

23.11.6.a.m: Milk from four teats, from three teats, from two teats, and from one teat—thus are the fast milks for three months each.

23.11.8.a.m: By means of the Twelve-Year sacrifice of Prajāpati they prosper with the prosperity of Prajāpati.

23.11.9.a.m: Three trivṛt years, three pañcadaśa, three saptadaśa, and three ekaviṃśa.

23.11.10.a.m: Those desiring heaven should undertake this very same [course] of the Naimiṣīyas.

23.11.11.a.s: nava trivṛtaḥ saṃvatsarā nava pañcadaśā nava saptadaśā navikaviṃśāḥ śāktyānāṃ ṣaṭtriṃśatsaṃvatsaraṃ tarasapuroḍāśaṃ kāpyādhvaryavamāgastyagṛhapatikam
23.11.11.a.d: नव त्रिवृतः संवत्सरा नव पञ्चदशा नव सप्तदशा नविकविंशाः शाक्त्यानां षट्त्रिंशत्संवत्सरं तरसपुरोडाशं काप्याध्वर्यवमागस्त्यगृहपतिकम्
23.11.11.a.m: Nine trivṛt years, nine pañcadaśa, nine saptadaśa, and nine ekaviṃśa belong to the thirty-six-year sacrifice of the Śāktyas, having flesh cakes, Kāpya as adhvaryu, and Agastya as householder.

23.11.12.a.m: As each day concludes, the householder goes hunting.

23.11.13.a.s: sa yānmṛgānhanti teṣāṃ tarasāḥ puroḍāśā bhavanti
23.11.13.a.d: स यान्मृगान्हन्ति तेषां तरसाः पुरोडाशा भवन्ति
23.11.13.a.m: The flesh of the wild beasts he slays becomes the sacrificial cakes.

23.11.14.a.s: etena ha vai śāktyo gaurivītistarasapuroḍāśa ārdhnoddevaloke ca manuṣyaloke carddhimṛdhnuvanti
23.11.14.a.d: एतेन ह वै शाक्त्यो गौरिवीतिस्तरसपुरोडाश आर्ध्नोद्देवलोके च मनुष्यलोके चर्द्धिमृध्नुवन्ति
23.11.14.a.m: By means of this indeed, Gaurīvīti Śāktya prospered with the meat-cake [sacrifice]; and they prosper with prosperity in the world of the gods and in the world of men.

23.11.15.a.s: pañcaviṃśatistrivṛtaḥ saṃvatsarāḥ pañcaviṃśatiḥ pañcadaśāḥ pañcaviṃśatiḥ saptadaśāḥ pañcaviṃśatirekaviṃśāḥ
23.11.15.a.d: पञ्चविंशतिस्त्रिवृतः संवत्सराः पञ्चविंशतिः पञ्चदशाः पञ्चविंशतिः सप्तदशाः पञ्चविंशतिरेकविंशाः
23.11.15.a.m: There are twenty-five ninefold years, twenty-five fifteenfold, twenty-five seventeenfold, and twenty-five twenty-onefold.

23.12.1.a.s: sādhyānāṃ śatasaṃvatsareṇa sagavāḥ sapuruṣāḥ svargaṃ lokaṃ yanti
23.12.1.a.d: साध्यानां शतसंवत्सरेण सगवाः सपुरुषाः स्वर्गं लोकं यन्ति
23.12.1.a.m: By means of the hundred-year [sacrifice] of the Sādhyas, they go to the heavenly world together with their cattle and with their men.

23.12.2.a.m: By means of the thousand-[day]-pressing [sacrifice] of Agni, they attain the production of all food.

23.12.3.a.m: There is an Atirātra, a thousand ninefold days, and an Atirātra.

23.12.4.a.m: There are three Sarasvatī sacrificial sessions.

23.12.4.b.m: The first belongs to Mitra and Varuṇa, the second to Indra and Agni, and the third to Aryaman.

23.12.5.a.m: They undergo consecration at the disappearance-place of the Sarasvatī.

23.12.6.a.m: Having performed the introductory sacrifice, purchased King [Soma], and tied him up, they deposit [him].

23.12.7.a.m: Having performed twelve upasads and undertaken the introductory Atirātra, on that day they keep away the calves.

23.12.8.a.m: When the introductory [Atirātra] is completed, they sacrifice with the curd-and-milk oblation.

23.12.9.a.m: When that is completed, the adhvaryu hurls the yoke-pin eastward.

23.12.10.a.m: Where it falls down, that is the gārhapatya.

23.12.11.a.m: From that, he strides thirty-six steps eastward.

23.12.13.a.m: The sadas, the havirdhāna [sheds], and the āgnīdhra [shed] have wheels.

23.12.14.a.m: The havirdhāna [shed] and the āgnīdhra [shed] are made of aśvattha wood.

23.12.15.a.m: The sacrificial post, whose bottom is like a mortar, is dragged along and merely set in the ground.

23.12.17.a.s: ta etam āpūryamāṇapakṣam āmāvāsyena haviṣā yānti
23.12.17.a.d: त एतम् आपूर्यमाणपक्षम् आमावास्येन हविषा यान्ति
23.12.17.a.m: They advance along this waxing half of the month with the new-moon oblation.

23.12.18.a.m: On the full moon, they undertake the Goṣṭoma having the Bṛhat sāman.

23.12.19.a.m: When that is completed, they sacrifice with the full-moon oblation.

23.12.20.a.m: They advance along this waning half of the month with the full-moon oblation.

23.12.21.a.m: On the new moon, they undertake the Āyuṣṭoma having the Rathaṃtara sāman.

23.12.22.a.m: When that is completed, they sacrifice with the curd-and-milk oblation.

23.12.23.a.s: ta evameva vyatyāsaṃ sarasvatyā dakṣiṇena kūlena
23.12.23.a.d: त एवमेव व्यत्यासं सरस्वत्या दक्षिणेन कूलेन
23.12.23.a.m: In just this way, alternately along the southern bank of the Sarasvatī,

23.13.2.a.m: At the confluence of the Dṛṣadvatī, having offered a mess of cooked food to Apāṃ Napāt, they pass beyond.

23.13.3.a.m: Among ten cows, [or] among a hundred, they let loose a bull.

23.13.4.a.s: yadā daśaśataṃ kurvantyathaikamutthānaṃ yadā vā śataṃ sahasram /
23.13.4.a.d: यदा दशशतं कुर्वन्त्यथैकमुत्थानं यदा वा शतं सहस्रम् ।
23.13.4.a.m: When the ten make a hundred, then is one rising; or when the hundred make a thousand;

23.13.4.b.s: yadā vā gṛhapatirmriyeta yadā vā sarvasvaṃ jīyeranyadā vā plākṣaṃ prasravaṇaṃ prāpnuvanti
23.13.4.b.d: यदा वा गृहपतिर्म्रियेत यदा वा सर्वस्वं जीयेरन्यदा वा प्लाक्षं प्रस्रवणं प्राप्नुवन्ति
23.13.4.b.m:
or when the master of the house dies; or when they are deprived of all property; or when they reach Plakṣaprāsravaṇa.

Having reached Plakṣaprāsravaṇa, they offer a sacrifice to Agni Kāma.

23.13.6.a.s: tasyāmaśvāṃ puruṣīṃ ca dhenuke dattvā kārapacavaṃ prati yamunāmavabhṛthamabhyavayanti
23.13.6.a.d: तस्यामश्वां पुरुषीं च धेनुके दत्त्वा कारपचवं प्रति यमुनामवभृथमभ्यवयन्ति
23.13.6.a.m: At it, having given a mare and a woman as milch animals, they go down to the Yamunā towards Kārapacava for the final purificatory bath.

23.13.7.a.m: In the second [session], the Bṛhaspatisava is ninefold, and the Go and Āyus days are the belly of Indra.

23.13.8.a.m: They surpass other creatures and become most vigorous.

23.13.9.a.m: In the third, the Jyotiḥ, Gauḥ, and Āyus are the course, and the Viśvajit and Abhijit are the belly of Indra.

23.13.10.a.m: They ascend the path of Aryaman and go to the world of the gods.

23.13.11.a.m: In the [session] along the Dṛṣadvatī, without losing a cow, he should guard the cows of a brahmin for a year.

23.13.12.a.m: For a year, he should kindle fire at Vyarṇa Naitandhava.

23.13.13.a.m: Having established the fire at Pariṇah, he should cast the yoke-pin along the southern bank of the Dṛṣadvatī with an eight-pot-sherd cake to Agni.

23.13.14.a.m: He goes down to the Yamunā towards Triplakṣa for the final purificatory bath.

23.13.15.a.m: Then indeed he disappears from men.

23.14.1.a.m: By the Turāyaṇa, he prospers with all prosperity.

23.14.2.a.m: Without being consecrated, he puts on a black-antelope skin;

23.14.2.b.m: he prospers thereby with human prosperity.

23.14.3.a.m: By the ascetic heat he performs, [he prospers] with divine [prosperity].

23.14.4.a.m: His vow consists of the sacrificial remnants.

23.14.5.a.m: For a year, he offers sacrifices arranged according to the pressings:

23.14.5.b.d: आग्नेयो ऽष्टाकपाल ऐन्द्र एकादशकपालो वैश्वदेवो द्वादशकपालः
23.14.5.b.m: an eight-pot-sherd cake to Agni, an eleven-pot-sherd cake to Indra, and a twelve-pot-sherd cake to the All-gods.

23.14.8.a.m: By means of the sacrificial session of the serpents, they ward off old age;

23.14.8.b.m: their radiance becomes like that of the Ādityas.

23.14.9.a.m: Each year consists of sets of ten [days], the twelfth is the Viṣuvant.

23.14.10.a.m: The three-year Gavāmayana belongs to the Ādityas and the Aṅgirases.

23.14.11.a.s: prājātiṃ bhūmānaṃ gacchantyabhi svargaṃ lokaṃ jayanatyeṣu lokeṣu pratitiṣṭhanti
23.14.11.a.d: प्राजातिं भूमानं गच्छन्त्यभि स्वर्गं लोकं जयनत्येषु लोकेषु प्रतितिष्ठन्ति
23.14.11.a.m: They attain offspring and abundance, conquer the heavenly world, and are established in these worlds.

23.14.12.a.m: By means of the thousand-year [sacrifice] of Prajāpati, they prosper with the prosperity of Prajāpati.

23.14.13.a.m: There is an Atirātra, a thousand ninefold years, and an Atirātra.

23.14.14.a.s: pañca pañcāśatastrivṛtaḥ saṃvatsarāḥ pañca pañcāśataḥpañcadaśāḥ pañca pañcāśataḥ saptadaśāḥ pañca pañcāśata ekaviṃśā viśvasṛjāṃ sahasrasaṃvatsaram
23.14.14.a.d: पञ्च पञ्चाशतस्त्रिवृतः संवत्सराः पञ्च पञ्चाशतःपञ्चदशाः पञ्च पञ्चाशतः सप्तदशाः पञ्च पञ्चाशत एकविंशा विश्वसृजां सहस्रसंवत्सरम्
23.14.14.a.m: There are fifty-five ninefold years, fifty-five fifteenfold, fifty-five seventeenfold, and fifty-five twenty-onefold: this is the thousand-year [sacrifice] of the Viśvasṛjs.

23.14.15.a.m: By this, indeed, the Viśvasṛjs created this universe;

23.14.15.b.m: because they created the universe (viśva), therefore they are called the Viśvasṛjs.

23.14.15.c.m: The universe is propagated after them.

23.14.16.a.s: viśvasṛjaḥ prathamāḥ sattramāsata sahasrasamaṃ prasutena yantaḥ /
23.14.16.a.d: विश्वसृजः प्रथमाः सत्त्रमासत सहस्रसमं प्रसुतेन यन्तः ।
23.14.16.a.m: "The universe-creators were the first to sit for a sacrificial session, proceeding for a thousand years with pressed [soma].

23.14.16.b.s: tato ha jajñe bhuvanasya gopā hiraṇmayaḥ śakunir brahma nāmeti
23.14.16.b.d: ततो ह जज्ञे भुवनस्य गोपा हिरण्मयः शकुनिर् ब्रह्म नामेति
23.14.16.b.m: Thence indeed was born the guardian of the world, the golden bird, Brahman by name." [Thus it is said.]

23.14.17.a.s: brahmaṇaḥ sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ yanti ya etadupayanti ya etadupayanti
23.14.17.a.d: ब्रह्मणः सायुज्यं सलोकतां यन्ति य एतदुपयन्ति य एतदुपयन्ति
23.14.17.a.m: They attain union with Brahman and common world [with Brahman] who undertake this, who undertake this.

24.1.2.a.m: It belongs to the three social classes: the Brahmin, the Rājanya, and the Vaiśya.

24.1.3.a.m: It is enjoined by the three Vedas:

24.1.4.a.m: by the Ṛgveda, the Yajurveda, and the Sāmaveda.

24.1.5.a.m: The New and Full Moon sacrifices [are enjoined] by the Ṛgveda and the Yajurveda;

24.1.8.a.m: [The ritual acts are] performed loudly with the Ṛgveda and the Sāmaveda;

24.1.10.a.m: except in the case of the āśruta, the pratyāśruta, the pravara, dialogues, and ritual calls.

24.1.11.a.m: The sāmidhenī verses are to be recited intermediate [between loud and whisper].

24.1.12.a.m: In a low tone prior to the two butter portions, and at the morning pressing;

24.1.13.a.m: in a middle tone prior to the Sviṣṭakṛt, and at the midday pressing;

24.1.14.a.m: in a high tone in the remainder, and at the third pressing.

24.1.15.a.m: The continuous flow of voice [is modulated] in the same way.

24.1.20.a.m: By explicit rule or in case of conflict, another may perform [the action].

24.1.21.a.m: The priestly office belongs to Brahmins.

24.1.22.a.m: The fires of all rites are established only once.

24.1.23.a.m: When it is enjoined, "he offers," one should understand clarified butter [as the offering substance];

24.1.28.a.m: The utensils are maintained from the establishment [of the fires] until the end of life.

24.1.29.a.m: Their consecration takes place at each ritual framework.

24.1.30.a.m: The mantra and the brāhmaṇa are the authority for the sacrifice.

24.1.31.a.m: The name "Veda" applies to mantra and brāhmaṇa.

24.1.32.a.m: The brāhmaṇas are injunctions for ritual acts.

24.1.33.a.d: ब्राह्मणशेषो ऽर्थवादो निन्दा प्रशंसा परकृतिः पुराकल्पश्च
24.1.33.a.m: The remainder of the brāhmaṇa is explanatory statement, censure, praise, the actions of others, and ancient tradition.

24.1.35.a.m: Those not handed down [in the Veda] are not mantras, as in the cases of the pravara, the ūha, and the utterance of personal names;

24.1.36.a.m: and the sound of a chariot and the sound of a drum.

24.1.37.a.m: An occasion of suspension of study applies to the mantras in private study, but not during ritual action, because the purpose is different.

24.1.39.a.m: even those consisting of distinct actions involving a number [of repetitions].

24.1.40.a.m: And likewise in scratching, sleeping, crossing a river, raining down upon [oneself], and addressing impure things, when they are not separated by time;

24.1.41.a.m: in setting out, however, [a single mantra serves] until the purpose is accomplished;

24.1.42.a.m: and likewise in actions that are not directly contiguous.

24.1.43.a.m: Repetition of the haviṣkṛt-call, the adhrigu-formula, the puronuvākyā, and the manotā-verse [occurs] at different times.

24.1.44.a.m: By explicit rule, a single action may have multiple mantras.

24.2.1.a.m: One should make the beginnings of actions coincide with the ends of mantras.

24.2.2.a.m: In the case of the āghāra libation and the continuous stream, the contact is at the beginning [of the mantra].

24.2.4.a.m: One should know the end of the preceding [mantra] by the beginning of the following.

24.2.5.a.m: In duties of the hotṛ and duties of the sacrificer, there is combination [of multiple mantras];

24.2.6.a.m: option in the case of the yājyā and the anuvākyā;

24.2.8.a.m: In purchases, hirings, and consecrations, there is combination of materials.

24.2.9.a.m: After performing acts dedicated to Rudra, Rakṣases, Nirṛti, or the ancestors, or acts of cutting, piercing, casting away, or touching one's own body, one should touch water.

24.2.10.a.m: The sacred ground has its operations directed from the north.

24.2.11.a.m: One should not turn one's back to the fire;

24.2.14.a.m: One must not pass a sacrificial implement accompanied by a mantra around oneself.

24.2.15.a.s: prāgapavargāṇyudagapavargāṇi vā yajñopavītī pradakṣiṇaṃ daivāni karmāṇi karoti
24.2.15.a.d: प्रागपवर्गाण्युदगपवर्गाणि वा यज्ञोपवीती प्रदक्षिणं दैवानि कर्माणि करोति
24.2.15.a.m: Wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder, moving clockwise, one performs rites for the gods ending towards the east or ending towards the north.

24.2.16.a.m: Wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder, moving counter-clockwise, rites for the ancestors end towards the south.

24.2.17.a.s: yāni śulbāni samāsaṃ gacchanti prasavyaṃ tānyāveṣṭya pradakṣiṇaṃ samasyet
24.2.17.a.d: यानि शुल्बानि समासं गच्छन्ति प्रसव्यं तान्यावेष्ट्य प्रदक्षिणं समस्येत्
24.2.17.a.m: Regarding cords that are combined together: having twisted them counter-clockwise, one should combine them clockwise.

24.2.18.a.s: atha yāni na samasyante pradakṣiṇaṃ tāni
24.2.18.a.d: अथ यानि न समस्यन्ते प्रदक्षिणं तानि
24.2.18.a.m: Now, those that are not combined are [twisted] clockwise.

24.2.19.a.m: One should sacrifice on the new moon day with the New Moon sacrifice,

24.2.20.a.m: on the full moon day with the Full Moon sacrifice.

24.2.21.a.m: On the day when the full moon rises in the east, on that full moon day one should observe the fast,

24.2.23.a.m: The Vājasaneyins recite [the view that it is on] the third, dwarfed [moon].

24.2.24.a.m: On the day when it is not seen, that day is the new moon day;

24.2.26.a.m: When primary rites are enjoined in a single context, they have the same procedure.

24.2.28.a.m: When there is no specific mention, they are common [to all];

24.2.29.a.m: due to specific mention, they are distributed.

24.2.30.a.d: आग्नेयो ऽष्टाकपालो ऽग्नीषोमीय एकादशकपाल उपांशुयाजश्च पौर्णमास्यां प्रधानानि
24.2.30.a.m: The cake on eight potsherds for Agni, the cake on eleven potsherds for Agni-Soma, and the whisper-offering are the primary rites on the full moon day.

24.2.32.a.d: आग्नेयो ऽष्टाकपाल ऐन्द्राग्न एकादशकपालो द्वादशकपालो वामावास्यायामसोमयाजिनः
24.2.32.a.m: The cake on eight potsherds for Agni, and a cake on eleven or twelve potsherds for Indra-Agni are [the primary rites] on the new moon day for one who has not performed a soma sacrifice.

24.2.33.a.m: The saṃnāyya is the second [primary rite] for one who has performed a soma sacrifice.

24.2.34.a.m: For a brahmin who has not performed a soma sacrifice, there is no sacrificial cake for Agni-Soma.

24.2.35.a.m: For one offering the saṃnāyya, there is no [cake] for Indra-Agni, without distinction of caste.

24.2.36.a.m: The sacrifice to the ancestors should not be an auxiliary rite, because its time is separately enjoined,

24.2.37.a.m: because it is enumerated as equivalent,

24.2.38.a.m: and because it is seen even when [the main sacrifice] is prohibited.

24.3.1.a.s: deśe kāle kartarīti nirdiśyate svaśabdaṃ yat
24.3.1.a.d: देशे काले कर्तरीति निर्दिश्यते स्वशब्दं यत्
24.3.1.a.m: whatever is expressly designated with regard to place, time, or agent [belongs to both].

24.3.6.a.m: or in a series of oblations, having scooped [the oblation] for each oblation,

24.3.8.a.m: and there is absence of kindling-stick, except in the agnihotra.

24.3.9.a.m: West of the fire, having bent the right knee or without bending it, seated, one offers the ladle-offerings,

24.3.11.a.m: Passing to the south behind the āhavanīya, facing north, one offers all oblations,

24.3.13.a.s: āśrutapratyāśrute yājyānuvākye avadāneṣu copastaraṇābhighāraṇe caturgṛhītaṃ vaṣaṭkāraścādarvihomānām
24.3.13.a.d: आश्रुतप्रत्याश्रुते याज्यानुवाक्ये अवदानेषु चोपस्तरणाभिघारणे चतुर्गृहीतं वषट्कारश्चादर्विहोमानाम्
24.3.13.a.m: The call and counter-call, the invitatory and consecratory verses, the under-spreading and dripping [of butter] upon the cut portions, the fourfold scooping, and the vaṣaṭ-call belong to non-ladle-offerings.

24.3.14.a.m: At the vaṣaṭ-call, or along with the vaṣaṭ-call, one should make [the oblation] fall into the offerings;

24.3.17.a.m: In a group of sacrificial cakes, one should divide off each one with the mantra, 'Divide according to your portions!';

24.3.18.a.m: the last two with, 'Divide, you two, according to your portions!'

24.3.19.a.m: He designates the deities for those two alone.

24.3.20.a.m: In a group of boiled mess and sacrificial cake, he separates what is for the boiled mess and what is for the sacrificial cake before pouring [the grains] out;

24.3.21.a.m: he designates them according to their deities.

24.3.22.a.m: The word 'idam' ('this') should be the common form,

24.3.24.a.m: At the time of placing the potsherds, he places the pot for the boiled mess with the first potsherd-mantra.

24.3.25.a.m: He modifies the mantra as 'dhruvo 'si' ('Firm art thou').

24.3.26.a.m: At the time of purifying the flour, he purifies the rice grains.

24.3.27.a.m: At the time of putting [the potsherds] on the fire, he pours in the rice grains with the putting-on mantra.

24.3.28.a.m: Without taking it out [of the pot], he sets down the boiled mess.

24.3.29.a.m: There are fifteen kindling verses in the New and Full Moon sacrifices;

24.3.30.a.m: seventeen in the animal sacrifices and optional sacrifices wherever they are prescribed.

24.3.31.a.s: upāṃśu kāmyā iṣṭayaḥ kriyanta iti tatra yāvatpradhānamupāṃśu
24.3.31.a.d: उपांशु काम्या इष्टयः क्रियन्त इति तत्र यावत्प्रधानमुपांशु
24.3.31.a.m: Where it is said, 'The optional sacrifices are performed in a whisper,' as much as is primary is [performed] in a whisper.

24.3.32.a.m: The New and Full Moon sacrifices are the archetype of the [other] sacrifices.

24.3.33.a.m: And [they are the archetype] of the animal [sacrifice] for Agni and Soma.

24.3.35.a.m: The savanīya [animal sacrifice is the archetype] of the group of eleven [animal sacrifices].

24.3.36.a.m: The group of eleven [animal sacrifices is the archetype] of animal groups.

24.3.37.a.m: The Vaiśvadeva [parvan is the archetype] of the Varuṇapraghāsa, Sākamedha, and Śunāsīrīya [parvans].

24.3.38.a.m: The single-potsherd [cake] belonging to the Vaiśvadeva is [the archetype] of [all] single-potsherd [cakes].

24.3.39.a.m: The curd mixture belonging to the Vaiśvadeva is [the archetype] of curd mixtures.

24.3.40.a.m: In that case, the modification should be understood from similarity.

24.3.41.a.m: Those [offerings] with a single deity are modifications of the [cake] for Agni.

24.3.42.a.m: Those with two deities are modifications of the [cake] for Agni and Soma.

24.3.45.a.m: [This applies] when [the deities] are other than the deities of the archetype, as: "a sacrificial cake for Indra, a cooked mess of rice for Soma."

24.3.46.a.m: When there is similarity both of the sacrificial substance and of the deity, the sacrificial substance is stronger.

24.3.47.a.m: When there is a conflict between substance and consecration, the substance is stronger.

24.3.48.a.m: When there is a conflict between purpose and substance, the purpose is stronger.

24.3.49.a.m: In the archetype, there is no modification [of mantras].

24.3.50.a.m: In an ectypal rite, there is modification according to the purpose, except for an explanatory remark.

24.3.51.a.m: An explanatory remark is due to the hearing of another sentence.

24.3.52.a.m: In the absence of what has been prescribed, a substitute [is adopted] on the basis of similarity.

24.3.54.a.m: If there is a deficiency in quantity, one should complete it with the remainder of that [same substance].

24.4.1.a.m: A substitute is excluded in the case of the master [of the sacrifice], the fire, the deity, from the [authoritative] word, and because of a prohibition of the ritual action.

24.4.2.a.m: The archetype ceases due to three causes: due to replacement, due to prohibition, and due to cessation of the purpose.

24.4.3.a.m: The Agniṣṭoma is the archetype of one-day rites.

24.4.5.a.m: The Gavāmayana [is the archetype] of year-long rites.

24.4.6.a.m: And of the series [of identical rites], the first [is the archetype].

24.4.7.a.m: At the Agniṣṭoma, there is a high altar.

24.4.8.a.m: In subsequent sacrifices, there is the piling of the fire;

24.4.9.a.m: except in the case of the Sādyaskra rites, the Vājapeya, the Ṣoḍaśin, and the Sārasvata sattra.

24.4.10.a.m: At the beginning of a sacrifice, one should desire the desire of the sacrifice.

24.4.11.a.m: At the beginning of a subordinate part of the sacrifice, [one should desire] the desire of the subordinate part of the sacrifice.

24.4.12.a.s: alpīyāṃso mantrā bhūyāṃsi karmāṇi tatra samaśaḥ prativibhajya pūrvaiḥ pūrvāṇi kārayeduttarairuttarāṇi
24.4.12.a.d: अल्पीयांसो मन्त्रा भूयांसि कर्माणि तत्र समशः प्रतिविभज्य पूर्वैः पूर्वाणि कारयेदुत्तरैरुत्तराणि
24.4.12.a.m: When there are fewer mantras and more ritual actions, having divided them equally there, one should cause the earlier [actions] to be performed with the earlier [mantras] and the later [actions] with the later [mantras].

24.4.13.a.s: alpīyāṃsi karmāṇi bhūyāṃso mantrāstatra pratimantraṃ kuryāt /
24.4.13.a.d: अल्पीयांसि कर्माणि भूयांसो मन्त्रास्तत्र प्रतिमन्त्रं कुर्यात् ।
24.4.13.a.m: When there are fewer ritual actions and more mantras, one should perform [an action] to each mantra;

24.4.13.b.m: the remaining ones serve the purpose of option, as [in the case of] the substances for the sacrificial post.

24.4.14.a.m: Omission or addition [takes place] from the end.

24.4.15.a.m: Because the archetypal [ritual element] is mentioned earlier, the un-archetypal should be at the end.

24.4.16.a.m: Because of the sufficiency of the pot, the spit, and the omentum-roasting spit, there should be a common performance.

24.4.17.a.m: If there is a difference of species, however, it should be divided, because of the inequality of cooking.

24.4.18.a.s: sviṣṭakṛdvikāre vanaspatau yājyāyāṃ devatānigamāḥ syuḥ prakṛtyupabandhāt
24.4.18.a.d: स्विष्टकृद्विकारे वनस्पतौ याज्यायां देवतानिगमाः स्युः प्रकृत्युपबन्धात्
24.4.18.a.m: In the case of Vanaspati as a modification of Sviṣṭakṛt, the mentions of the deities should occur in the consecratory verse, because of the connection with the archetype.

24.4.19.a.m: The initial offering should not occur in an ectypal rite, because it is within the time of the archetypal rite;

24.4.20.a.m: Or rather, it should occur, because the time is not an accessory part,

24.4.22.a.m: For each distinct purpose, one brings forward the fire.

24.4.22.b.s: apavṛtte karmaṇi laukikaḥ saṃpadyate yathā samārūḍhe
24.4.22.b.d: अपवृत्ते कर्मणि लौकिकः संपद्यते यथा समारूढे
24.4.22.b.m: When the ritual action has ended, it becomes profane, as when it has mounted [the two kindling sticks].

24.5.1.a.m: We shall explain the ancestral lineage invocations.

24.5.2.b.m: "he does not depart from kinship; furthermore, for continuity," so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

24.5.3.a.m: He chooses the ancestral seer lineage neither by gods nor by humans;

24.5.3.b.m: "he chooses the ancestral seer lineage only by the seers," so it is known.

24.5.4.b.s: ṛṣiṇā hi devāḥ puruṣamanubudhyanta iti vijñāyate
24.5.4.b.d: ऋषिणा हि देवाः पुरुषमनुबुध्यन्त इति विज्ञायते
24.5.4.b.m: "for by means of the seer the gods recognise a man," so it is known.

24.5.5.a.s: yo vā anyaḥ sannathānyasyārṣeyeṇa pravṛṇīte sa vā asya tadṛṣiriṣṭaṃ vītaṃ vṛṅktaṃ iti vijñāyate
24.5.5.a.d: यो वा अन्यः सन्नथान्यस्यार्षेयेण प्रवृणीते स वा अस्य तदृषिरिष्टं वीतं वृङ्क्तं इति विज्ञायते
24.5.5.a.m: "Whoever, being one person, then chooses [his lineage] with the ancestral seers of another, that seer of his deprives him of what has been sacrificed and what has been given," so it is known.

24.5.6.c.m: "according to the seer, he chooses the mantra-makers," so it is known.

24.5.7.f.m: he does not choose beyond five—so it is known from the tradition.

24.5.8.a.d: अत ऊर्ध्वानध्वर्युर्वृणीते ऽमुतो ऽर्वाचो होतेति विज्ञायते
24.5.8.a.m: The adhvaryu chooses them upwards from here; the hotṛ downwards from there—so it is known from the tradition.

24.5.9.a.s: purohitasya pravareṇa rājā pravṛṇita iti vijñāyate
24.5.9.a.d: पुरोहितस्य प्रवरेण राजा प्रवृणित इति विज्ञायते
24.5.9.a.m: A king chooses with the ancestral formula (pravara) of his domestic priest—so it is known from the tradition.

24.5.10.a.m: We shall explain [the ancestral invocations] of the Bhṛgus first.

24.5.12.a.m: theirs is a five-seer ancestral formula (pravara):

24.5.12.b.m: 'O descendant of Bhṛgu, of Cyavana, of Apnavāna, of Ūrva, of Jamadagni!'—

24.5.12.c.m: 'Like Jamadagni, like Ūrva, like Apnavāna, like Cyavana, like Bhṛgu!'

24.5.13.b.m: 'O descendant of Bhṛgu, of Ūrva, of Jamadagni!'—

24.5.14.a.m: This very one unmodified belongs to the Sāvarṇis, Jīvantis, Jābālis, Aitiśāyanas, Vairohityas, Avaṭas, Maṇḍus, and Prācīnayogyas.

24.5.15.a.m: Now for the Ārṣṭiṣeṇas, there is a five-seer ancestral formula:

24.5.15.b.m: 'O descendant of Bhṛgu, of Cyavana, of Apnavāna, of Ṛṣṭiṣeṇa, of Anūpa!'—

24.5.15.c.m: 'Like Anūpa, like Ṛṣṭiṣeṇa, like Apnavāna, like Cyavana, like Bhṛgu!'

24.5.16.b.m: 'O descendant of Bhṛgu, of Ṛṣṭiṣeṇa, of Anūpa!'—

24.6.1.a.m: Now the Vītahavyas: the Yāskas, Vādhūlas, and Maunamaukas:

24.6.2.b.m: 'O descendant of Bhṛgu, of Vītahavya, of Savedas!'—

24.6.8.b.m: 'O descendant of Bhṛgu, of Vena, of Pṛthu!'—

24.6.10.a.m: Now then of the Aṅgirases: the Āyāsya Gautamas:

24.6.11.b.m: 'O descendant of Aṅgiras, of Ayāsya, of Gotama!'

24.6.13.b.m: 'O descendant of Aṅgiras, of Ucathya, of Gotama!'—

24.6.15.b.m: 'O descendant of Aṅgiras, of Uśij, of Kakṣīvat!'—

24.6.17.b.m: 'O descendant of Aṅgiras, of Vāmadeva, of Bṛhaduktha!'—

24.6.18.a.m: Now for the Bharadvājas, there is a three-seer ancestral formula:

24.6.18.b.m: 'O descendant of Aṅgiras, of Bṛhaspati, of Bharadvāja!'—

24.7.1.a.m: [belongs] to the Kukvas, the Agniveśyas, the Ūrjāyanas, and all those named Stambastamba.

24.7.2.a.m: Now, of families of dual lineage (dvyāmuṣyāyaṇa), such as the Śuṅga-Śiśiras:

24.7.4.b.m: “O descendant of Aṅgiras, descendant of Bṛhaspati, descendant of Bharadvāja, descendant of Kata, descendant of Atkīla!”

24.7.4.c.m: [and in the hotṛ’s formula:] “Like Atkīla, like Kata, like Bharadvāja, like Bṛhaspati, like Aṅgiras!”

24.7.5.b.m: “O descendant of Aṅgiras, descendant of Kata, descendant of Atkīla!”

24.7.6.a.m: Now, for the Ṛkṣas, there is a five-seer [pravara]:

24.7.6.b.m: “O descendant of Aṅgiras, descendant of Bṛhaspati, descendant of Bharadvāja, descendant of Vandana, descendant of Matavacasa!”

24.7.6.c.m: “Like Matavacasa, like Vandana, like Bharadvāja, like Bṛhaspati, like Aṅgiras!”

24.7.7.b.m: “O descendant of Aṅgiras, descendant of Vandana, descendant of Matavacasa!”

24.7.8.a.m: Now, for the Kapis, there is a three-seer [pravara]:

24.7.8.b.m: “O descendant of Aṅgiras, descendant of Āmahīyu, descendant of Urukṣaya!”

24.7.9.a.m: Now, for the Gargas, there is a three-seer [pravara]:

24.7.9.b.m: “O descendant of Aṅgiras, descendant of Garga, descendant of Śini!”

24.7.10.a.m: Some indeed [prescribe] Bharadvāja in place of Aṅgiras:

24.7.10.b.m: “O descendant of Bharadvāja, descendant of Garga, descendant of Śini!”

24.7.11.a.m: Now, for the Haritas, there is a three-seer [pravara]:

24.7.11.b.m: “O descendant of Aṅgiras, descendant of Ambarīṣa, descendant of Yuvanāśva!”

24.7.12.a.m: Some indeed [prescribe] Māndhātṛ in place of Aṅgiras:

24.7.12.b.m: “O descendant of Māndhātṛ, descendant of Ambarīṣa, descendant of Yuvanāśva!”

24.8.1.a.m: Now, for the Kutsas, there is a three-seer [pravara]:

24.8.1.b.m: “O descendant of Aṅgiras, descendant of Māndhātṛ, descendant of Kutsa!”

24.8.3.b.m: “O descendant of Aṅgiras, descendant of Ajamīḍha, descendant of Kaṇva!”

24.8.4.a.m: Now, the Rathītaras who are Virūpas:

24.8.5.b.m: “O descendant of Aṅgiras, descendant of Virūpa, descendant of Pṛṣadaśva!”

24.8.6.a.m: Some indeed [prescribe] Aṣṭrādaṃṣṭra in place of Aṅgiras:

24.8.6.b.m: “O descendant of Aṣṭrādaṃṣṭra, descendant of Virūpa, descendant of Pṛṣadaśva!”

24.8.7.a.m: Now, for the Mudgalas, there is a three-seer [pravara]:

24.8.7.b.m: “O descendant of Aṅgiras, descendant of Bhṛmyaśva, descendant of Mudgala!”

24.8.8.a.m: Some indeed [prescribe] Tṛkṣa in place of Aṅgiras:

24.8.8.b.m: “O descendant of Tṛkṣa, descendant of Bhṛmyaśva, descendant of Mudgala!”

24.8.9.a.m: Now, for the Viṣṇuvṛddhas, there is a three-seer [pravara]:

24.8.9.b.m: “O descendant of Aṅgiras, descendant of Purukutsa, descendant of Trasadasyu!”

24.8.10.a.m: This very same [pravara remains] unmodified for the Śaṭhamarṣaṇas, Bhadraṇas, Madraṇas, Bādarāyaṇas, Aupamanyus, Aupagavis, Sātyakis, Sātyaṃkāmis, Āruṇis, and Nituṇḍis.

24.8.11.a.m: Now, for the Atris, there is a three-seer [pravara]:

24.8.11.b.m: “O descendant of Atri, descendant of Arcanānas, descendant of Śyāvāśva!”

24.8.12.a.m: Now, for the Gaviṣṭhiras, there is a three-seer [pravara]:

24.8.12.b.m: “O descendant of Atri, descendant of Arcanānas, descendant of Gaviṣṭhira!”

24.8.13.a.m: Now, for the Atithis, there are three ancestral seers:

24.8.13.c.m: [the adhvaryu says:] 'Like Atithi, like Arcanānas, like Atri!'

24.8.14.a.m: This very [pravara], unmodified, belongs to the Vāmarathyas, Sumaṅgalas, and Baijavāpis.

24.9.1.a.m: Now, among the Viśvāmitras: the Devarātas, Cikitās, Manutantus, Aulakis, Vālukis, Yajñavalkas, Ulūkas, Bṛhadagnis, Babhrus, Gālavas, Śālāvata-Śālaṅkāyanas, and Kālabavas.

24.9.2.b.m: [the hotṛ says:] 'O descendant of Viśvāmitra, of Devarāta, of Udala!'

24.9.2.c.m: [the adhvaryu says:] 'Like Udala, like Devarāta, like Viśvāmitra!'

24.9.3.a.m: Now, of the Śraumata-Kāmakāyanas, there is a three-ṛṣi invocation:

24.9.3.b.m: [the hotṛ says:] 'O descendant of Viśvāmitra, of Devaśravas, of Devataras!'

24.9.3.c.m: [the adhvaryu says:] 'Like Devataras, like Devaśravas, like Viśvāmitra!'

24.9.4.a.m: Now, of the Ājyas, there is a three-ṛṣi invocation:

24.9.4.b.m: [the hotṛ says:] 'O descendant of Viśvāmitra, of Madhucchandas, of Aja!'

24.9.4.c.m: [the adhvaryu says:] 'Like Aja, like Madhucchandas, like Viśvāmitra!'

24.9.5.a.m: Now, the Dhanaṃjayas are indeed descendants of Madhucchandas.

24.9.6.b.m: [the hotṛ says:] 'O descendant of Viśvāmitra, of Madhucchandas, of Dhanaṃjaya!'

24.9.6.c.m: [the adhvaryu says:] 'Like Dhanaṃjaya, like Madhucchandas, like Viśvāmitra!'

24.9.10.b.m: [the hotṛ says:] 'O descendant of Viśvāmitra, of Pūraṇa!'

24.9.11.a.m: Now, of the Katas, there is a three-ṛṣi invocation:

24.9.11.b.m: [the hotṛ says:] 'O descendant of Viśvāmitra, of Kata, of Atkīla!'

24.9.11.c.m: [the adhvaryu says:] 'Like Atkīla, like Kata, like Viśvāmitra!'

24.9.13.b.m: [the hotṛ says:] 'O descendant of Viśvāmitra, of Aghamarṣaṇa, of Kuśika!'

24.9.13.c.m: [the adhvaryu says:] 'Like Kuśika, like Aghamarṣaṇa, like Viśvāmitra!'

24.9.14.a.m: Now, of the Kaśyapas, there is a three-ṛṣi invocation:

24.9.14.b.m: [the hotṛ says:] 'O descendant of Kaśyapa, of Avatsāra, of Nidhruva!'

24.9.14.c.m: [the adhvaryu says:] 'Like Nidhruva, like Avatsāra, like Kaśyapa!'

24.9.15.a.m: Now, of the Rebhas, there is a three-ṛṣi invocation:

24.9.15.b.m: [the hotṛ says:] 'O descendant of Kaśyapa, of Avatsāra, of Rebha!'

24.9.15.c.m: [the adhvaryu says:] 'Like Rebha, like Avatsāra, like Kaśyapa!'

24.10.1.a.m: Now, of the Śaṇḍilas, there is a two-ṛṣi invocation:

24.10.2.b.m: [the hotṛ says:] 'O descendant of Kaśyapa, of Devala, of Asita!'

24.10.2.c.m: [the adhvaryu says:] 'Like Asita, like Devala, like Kaśyapa!'

24.10.3.a.m: By rule, however, they have a two-ṛṣi invocation.

24.10.4.a.m: The Vāsiṣṭhas have a one-ṛṣi invocation, except for the Parāśaras:

24.10.4.b.m: The hotṛ [says]: 'O descendant of Vasiṣṭha!'; the adhvaryu [says]: 'Like Vasiṣṭha!'

24.10.5.b.m: [the hotṛ says:] 'O descendant of Vasiṣṭha, of Indrapramada, of Ābharadvasu!'

24.10.5.c.m: [the adhvaryu says:] 'Like Ābharadvasu, like Indrapramada, like Vasiṣṭha!'

24.10.6.a.m: Now, of the Parāśaras, there is a three-ṛṣi invocation:

24.10.6.b.m: [the hotṛ says:] 'O descendant of Vasiṣṭha, of Śakti, of Parāśara!'

24.10.6.c.m: [the adhvaryu says:] 'Like Parāśara, like Śakti, like Vasiṣṭha!'

24.10.7.a.m: Now, of the Kuṇḍinas, there is a three-ṛṣi invocation:

24.10.7.b.m: [the hotṛ says:] 'O descendant of Vasiṣṭha, of Mitrāvaruṇa, of Kuṇḍina!'

24.10.7.c.m: [the adhvaryu says:] 'Like Kuṇḍina, like Mitrāvaruṇa, like Vasiṣṭha!'

24.10.8.a.m: Now, of the Saṃkṛtis and Pūtimāṣas, there is a three-ṛṣi invocation:

24.10.8.b.m: [the hotṛ says:] 'O descendant of Śakti, of Saṃkṛti, of Gaurivīti!'

24.10.8.c.m: [the adhvaryu says:] 'Like Gaurivīti, like Saṃkṛti, like Śakti!'

24.10.9.a.m: Now, of the Agastis, there is a one-ṛṣi invocation:

24.10.10.b.m: "O descendant of Agastya, O Dārḍhacyuta, O Idhmavāha," [says the hotṛ];

24.10.10.c.m: "like Idhmavāha, like Dṛḍhacyuta, like Agastya," [says the adhvaryu].

24.10.12.a.m: If they choose royal sovereignty, there is only one ancestral lineage for them:

24.10.12.b.m: "O descendant of Manu, O descendant of Iḍā, O descendant of Purūravas," [says the hotṛ];

24.10.12.c.m: "like Purūravas, like Iḍāvat, like Manu," [says the adhvaryu].

24.10.13.a.s: atha yeṣāmu ha mantrakṛto na syuḥ sapurohitapravarāste pravṛṇīran
24.10.13.a.d: अथ येषामु ह मन्त्रकृतो न स्युः सपुरोहितप्रवरास्ते प्रवृणीरन्
24.10.13.a.m: Now, for those who do not have hymn-composers [among their ancestors], they should choose having the ancestral lineage of their purohita.

24.10.14.a.m: Now, those who have [hymn-composers among their ancestors] do not have the ancestral lineage of their purohita.

24.10.15.a.m: However, by this principle, they [still] have the ancestral lineage of their purohita.

24.10.17.a.m: Now, one whose lineage is unknown should recite after the lineage of his teacher, [or] he should choose the ancestral lineage of his teacher.

24.10.18.a.m: Now the Tāṇḍins prescribe a single ṛṣi belonging to all classes:

24.10.18.d.s: mānavyo hi prajā iti hi brāhmaṇamiti hi brāhmaṇam
24.10.18.d.d: मानव्यो हि प्रजा इति हि ब्राह्मणमिति हि ब्राह्मणम्
24.10.18.d.m: For "creatures are descended from Manu," so indeed says the Brāhmaṇa; so indeed says the Brāhmaṇa.

24.11.1.a.s: purastātsāmidhenīnāṃ hotā hṛdayadeśa ūrdhvaṃ prādeśaṃ dhārayamāṇo japati mayi gṛhṇāmyagre agniṃ yo no agniḥ pitara iti
24.11.1.a.d: पुरस्तात्सामिधेनीनां होता हृदयदेश ऊर्ध्वं प्रादेशं धारयमाणो जपति मयि गृह्णाम्यग्रे अग्निं यो नो अग्निः पितर इति
24.11.1.a.m: Before the kindling verses, the hotṛ, holding an upright span at the region of his heart, mutters: "In me I take Agni first; he who is our fire, O fathers."

24.11.2.a.s: antarāhavanīyamutkaraṃ ca pratīcīnaṃ gacchañjapati kaṃ prapadye taṃ prapadye /
24.11.2.a.d: अन्तराहवनीयमुत्करं च प्रतीचीनं गच्छञ्जपति कं प्रपद्ये तं प्रपद्ये ।
24.11.2.a.m: Going westward between the āhavanīya and the rubbish heap, he mutters: "Whom do I enter? Him I enter.

24.11.2.b.m: That which is your refuge, your meter, O Prajāpati, that do I enter.

24.11.2.c.m: As much as I know of you, O Viṣṇu, so much will I do for you.

24.11.2.d.s: namo agnaya upadraṣṭre namo vāyava upaśrotre nama ādityāyānukhyātre /
24.11.2.d.d: नमो अग्नय उपद्रष्ट्रे नमो वायव उपश्रोत्रे नम आदित्यायानुख्यात्रे ।
24.11.2.d.m: Homage to Agni, the onlooker! Homage to Vāyu, the overhearer! Homage to Āditya, the overseer!

24.11.2.e.s: juṣṭāmadya devebhyo vācamudyāsaṃ svadhāvatīṃ pitṛbhyaḥ śuśrūṣeṇyāṃ manuṣyebhyaḥ /
24.11.2.e.d: जुष्टामद्य देवेभ्यो वाचमुद्यासं स्वधावतीं पितृभ्यः शुश्रूषेण्यां मनुष्येभ्यः ।
24.11.2.e.m: May I speak today speech pleasing to the gods, accompanied by svadhā for the fathers, worthy of being heard by men.

24.11.2.f.s: praśāsta ātmanā prajayā paśubhiḥ prajāpatiṃ prapadye /
24.11.2.f.d: प्रशास्त आत्मना प्रजया पशुभिः प्रजापतिं प्रपद्ये ।
24.11.2.f.m: Directing with myself, with offspring, with cattle, I enter Prajāpati.

24.11.2.h.m: I will recite what pertains to Prajāpati.

24.11.2.i.m: May speech perform the priest's duty; may mind perform the priest's duty.

24.11.2.j.m: I enter speech: bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ."

24.11.3.a.m: With "I stand in the place of Viṣṇu," he takes his stance.

24.11.4.a.m: The right foot is inside the altar ground;

24.11.5.a.s: athordhvastiṣṭhanbrahmansāmidhenīranuvakṣyāmīti brahmāṇamāmantrya daśahotāraṃ vyākhyāya vyāhṛtīśca japitvā trirhiṅkṛtottamena hiṅkāreṇārdharcamupasaṃdadhāti
24.11.5.a.d: अथोर्ध्वस्तिष्ठन्ब्रह्मन्सामिधेनीरनुवक्ष्यामीति ब्रह्माणमामन्त्र्य दशहोतारं व्याख्याय व्याहृतीश्च जपित्वा त्रिर्हिङ्कृतोत्तमेन हिङ्कारेणार्धर्चमुपसंदधाति
24.11.5.a.m: Then, standing upright, having addressed the brahman [priest] with "O brahman, I will recite the kindling verses," having recited the daśahotṛ formula and muttered the mystical utterances, having uttered hiṅ three times, he joins the half-verse with the final hiṅ-sound.

24.11.6.a.m: He recites the first [verse] three times, and the last three times.

24.11.7.a.s: yaṃ kāmayeta sarvamāyuriyāditi tasya triranavānaṃ prathamottame anubrūyāt
24.11.7.a.d: यं कामयेत सर्वमायुरियादिति तस्य त्रिरनवानं प्रथमोत्तमे अनुब्रूयात्
24.11.7.a.m: For one of whom he desires that he may attain the full lifespan, he should recite the first and last [verses] three times without taking a breath.

24.11.8.a.m: "Continuously connecting each single [verse], he should recite without taking a breath," say some.

24.11.9.a.m: He divides the third kindling verse three times.

24.11.9.b.m: "He recites continuously," since there is no distinction among the kindling verses.

24.11.10.b.m: "From various ṛṣis, indeed, are these kindling verses fashioned.

24.11.10.c.s: tā yadasaṃyuktāḥ syuḥ prajayā paśubhiryajamānasya vitiṣṭheran /
24.11.10.c.d: ता यदसंयुक्ताः स्युः प्रजया पशुभिर्यजमानस्य वितिष्ठेरन् ।
24.11.10.c.m: If they were unconnected, they would scatter with the offspring and cattle of the sacrificer.

24.11.10.d.s: ardharcau saṃdadhāti saṃyunaktyevainā iti te manyāmahe
24.11.10.d.d: अर्धर्चौ संदधाति संयुनक्त्येवैना इति ते मन्यामहे
24.11.10.d.m: He joins the two half-verses; he connects them indeed"—so we hold.

24.11.11.a.m: He should join the latter [half-verse] of the preceding [verse] and the former [half-verse] of the succeeding [verse].

24.11.12.a.m: The teaching that there is no taking of breath during the kindling verses is [from the text] "he recites continuously"; and it is known [from sacred text]:

24.11.13.b.m: If he should take breath between two verses, he would place the out-breath in the down-breath.

24.11.13.c.m: Passing over the [second] half-verse of the preceding [verse], he takes breath during the [first] half-verse of the succeeding [verse]."

24.11.14.a.m: The continuity of half-verses is found through reciting three times, because they have a single ṛṣi.

24.11.15.a.m: "You, O Varuṇa" is the concluding verse for the Vasiṣṭhas and the Rājanyas;

24.11.16.a.m: Narāśaṃsa is the second fore-offering for the Vasiṣṭhas and the Śunakas;

24.11.17.a.m: Having recited the kindling verses and having spoken the ancestral lineage, he recites the nivids.

24.11.18.a.m: Having spoken seven words of them, he takes breath;

24.12.2.a.s: tā anūcya devatā āvāhayati yā yakṣyamāṇo bhavati
24.12.2.a.d: ता अनूच्य देवता आवाहयति या यक्ष्यमाणो भवति
24.12.2.a.m: Having recited them, he invokes the deities to whom [the sacrificer] is about to sacrifice.

24.12.3.a.s: sa vai khalu vājino nāvāhayeddevikā devasuvo yacca kiṃ caitādṛkte manyāmahe
24.12.3.a.d: स वै खलु वाजिनो नावाहयेद्देविका देवसुवो यच्च किं चैतादृक्ते मन्यामहे
24.12.3.a.m: Indeed, he should not invoke the Vājins, the Devikās, the Devasūs, and whatever else is of such a kind, we consider.

24.12.4.a.m: There should be a prohibition of those subordinate to another and separated by another procedure, because the Vedic text indicates that.

24.12.5.a.m: For [offerings to] the same deity separated by [offerings to] different deities, the invocation is common, on account of adequacy.

24.12.6.a.s: athordhvajñuḥ prādeśena bhūmimabhinidhāya japatīdamahaṃ trivṛtā stomena rathaṃtareṇa sāmaṇ vaṣaṭkāreṇa vajreṇāsyai pṛthivyā asyai pratiṣṭhāyā asmādāyatanādyo 'smāndveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣmastaṃ hanmi //
24.12.6.a.d: अथोर्ध्वज्ञुः प्रादेशेन भूमिमभिनिधाय जपतीदमहं त्रिवृता स्तोमेन रथंतरेण सामण् वषट्कारेण वज्रेणास्यै पृथिव्या अस्यै प्रतिष्ठाया अस्मादायतनाद्यो ऽस्मान्द्वेष्टि यं च वयं द्विष्मस्तं हन्मि ॥
24.12.6.a.m: Then, with knee raised, having pressed the ground with a span [of his hand], he murmurs: "Here I strike him who hates us and whom we hate, from this earth, from this firm foundation, from this dwelling, with the trivṛt chant, with the rathaṃtara sāman, with the vaṣaṭ-call as a vajra!"

24.12.6.b.m: "If today in the choosing of the hotṛ the eye went astray crookedly,

24.12.6.c.m: Agni Jātavedas, who looks upon all men, brought it back!"

24.12.6.d.s: vasūnāṃ rātau syāma rudrāṇāmūrmyāyāṃ svādityā aditaye 'nehasaḥ /
24.12.6.d.d: वसूनां रातौ स्याम रुद्राणामूर्म्यायां स्वादित्या अदितये ऽनेहसः ।
24.12.6.d.m: "May we be in the bounty of the Vasus, in the surge of the Rudras, well-Adityas, sinless for Aditi!

24.12.6.e.s: cārumadya devebhyo vācamudyāsaṃ cāruṃ brahmabhyaścāruṃ manuṣyebhyaścāruṃ narāśaṃsāyānumatāṃ pitṛbhiḥ /
24.12.6.e.d: चारुमद्य देवेभ्यो वाचमुद्यासं चारुं ब्रह्मभ्यश्चारुं मनुष्येभ्यश्चारुं नराशंसायानुमतां पितृभिः ।
24.12.6.e.m: May I speak pleasant speech today to the gods, pleasant to the Brahmans, pleasant to men, pleasant to Narāśaṃsa, approved by the fathers!

24.12.6.f.s: ye te śataṃ varuṇa ye sahasraṃ yajñiyāḥ pāśā vitatāḥ purutrā /
24.12.6.f.d: ये ते शतं वरुण ये सहस्रं यज्ञियाः पाशा वितताः पुरुत्रा ।
24.12.6.f.m: Those hundred, O Varuṇa, those thousand sacrificial snares of yours stretched out far and wide,

24.12.6.g.s: tebhyo na indraḥ savitota viṣṇurviśve devā muñcantu marutaḥ svastyeti
24.12.6.g.d: तेभ्यो न इन्द्रः सवितोत विष्णुर्विश्वे देवा मुञ्चन्तु मरुतः स्वस्त्येति
24.12.6.g.m: from them let Indra, Savitṛ, and Viṣṇu, all the gods, the Maruts release us for well-being!"

24.12.7.a.s: atha yadenamāhāsau manuṣa iti tadupotthāya dakṣiṇena pāṇinā dakṣiṇāmadhvaryoraṃsamanvārabhya japati /
24.12.7.a.d: अथ यदेनमाहासौ मनुष इति तदुपोत्थाय दक्षिणेन पाणिना दक्षिणामध्वर्योरंसमन्वारभ्य जपति ।
24.12.7.a.m: Then, when [the adhvaryu] says to him: "Such a one, of human descent!", having stood up towards him, touching the right shoulder of the adhvaryu with his right hand, he murmurs:

24.12.7.b.m: with his left [hand], the right [shoulder] of the āgnīdhra.

24.12.7.c.m: "Sixty and ninety snares, O adhvaryu, are unfastened between the hotṛ and Agni;

24.12.7.d.s: sinanti pākamati dhīra etyṛtasya panthāmanveti hotā //
24.12.7.d.d: सिनन्ति पाकमति धीर एत्यृतस्य पन्थामन्वेति होता ॥
24.12.7.d.m: they bind the simpleton; the wise one goes beyond them; the hotṛ follows the path of ṛta."

24.12.7.e.m: "We take hold of Agni, who was placed in front at the choosing of the hotṛ,

24.12.7.f.m: by whom the divine Aṅgirases went to the highest heaven, the light!"

24.12.8.a.m: With "In me are out-breath and in-breath," having withdrawn both hands, he touches the chest region.

24.12.9.a.s: ā pṛṇoṣi saṃpṛṇa prajayā mā paśubhirāpṛṇetīdhmasaṃnahanāni mukhaṃ prati vidhūnute
24.12.9.a.d: आ पृणोषि संपृण प्रजया मा पशुभिरापृणेतीध्मसंनहनानि मुखं प्रति विधूनुते
24.12.9.a.m: With "You fill up, fill [me] up; do fill me up with offspring and cattle," he shakes the firewood-bindings toward his face.

24.12.10.a.s: athāpa upaspṛśyāgne naya supathā rāye asmān //
24.12.10.a.d: अथाप उपस्पृश्याग्ने नय सुपथा राये अस्मान् ॥
24.12.10.a.m: Then, having touched water, with "O Agni, lead us along the good path to wealth..."

24.12.10.b.s: ehyagna iha hotā ni ṣīdādabdhaḥ su puraetā bhavā naḥ /
24.12.10.b.d: एह्यग्न इह होता नि षीदादब्धः सु पुरएता भवा नः ।
24.12.10.b.m: "Come, O Agni, sit down here as hotṛ; undeceived, be a good leader before us;

24.12.10.c.s: avatāṃ mā rodasī viśvaminve yajā mahe saumanasāya devānityete ṛcau japnhotṛṣadanāya pravrajati
24.12.10.c.d: अवतां मा रोदसी विश्वमिन्वे यजा महे सौमनसाय देवानित्येते ऋचौ जप्न्होतृषदनाय प्रव्रजति
24.12.10.c.m: may the two all-invigorating world-halves protect me; let us sacrifice to the gods for great benevolence!"—murmuring these two verses, he advances to the hotṛ's seat.

24.12.11.a.s: jaghanena hotṛṣadanaṃ prāṅmukha upaviśyātha hotṛṣadanamabhimṛśatyahe daidhiṣavyeti
24.12.11.a.d: जघनेन होतृषदनं प्राङ्मुख उपविश्याथ होतृषदनमभिमृशत्यहे दैधिषव्येति
24.12.11.a.m: Having sat down behind the hotṛ's seat facing east, he touches the hotṛ's seat with: "O Daidhiṣavya..."

24.12.12.a.m: Then he tosses away a blade of grass from it;

24.13.1.a.s: śuṣkaṃ pracchinnāgraṃ vā nirastaḥ parāgvasuḥ saha pāpmaneti
24.13.1.a.d: शुष्कं प्रच्छिन्नाग्रं वा निरस्तः पराग्वसुः सह पाप्मनेति
24.13.1.a.m: a dry one, or one whose tip is cut off, with: "Cast away is Parāgvasu together with evil!"

24.13.2.a.s: atha hotṛṣadana upaviśati pātaṃ mā dyāvāpṛthivī upastha iti dakṣiṇapūrviṇaṃ savyottariṇaṃ vopasthaṃ kṛtvā
24.13.2.a.d: अथ होतृषदन उपविशति पातं मा द्यावापृथिवी उपस्थ इति दक्षिणपूर्विणं सव्योत्तरिणं वोपस्थं कृत्वा
24.13.2.a.m: Then he sits down upon the hotṛ's seat, with: "Protect me, Heaven and Earth, in your lap!", having made his lap with the right [foot] first or with the left [foot] above.

24.13.3.a.s: atha japati sīda hotarni hotā hotṛṣadana iti dve //
24.13.3.a.d: अथ जपति सीद होतर्नि होता होतृषदन इति द्वे ॥
24.13.3.a.m: Then he murmurs the two: "Sit down, O hotṛ..." and "Down the hotṛ in the hotṛ's seat...";

24.13.3.b.m: this one: "Please the eager gods, O youngest one!";

24.13.3.c.s: veṣi hotramuta potraṃ janānāṃ mandhātāsi draviṇodā ṛtāvā /
24.13.3.c.d: वेषि होत्रमुत पोत्रं जनानां मन्धातासि द्रविणोदा ऋतावा ।
24.13.3.c.m: "You perform the hotṛ's office and the potṛ's office of the people; you are Mandhātṛ, the giver of wealth, the upholder of ṛta;

24.13.3.d.s: svāhā vayaṃ kṛṇavāmā havīṃṣi devo devānyajatyagnirarhan //
24.13.3.d.d: स्वाहा वयं कृणवामा हवींषि देवो देवान्यजत्यग्निरर्हन् ॥
24.13.3.d.m: svāhā! we would make the oblations; the god Agni, being worthy, sacrifices to the gods!"

24.13.3.i.s: viśveṣāṃ hyadhvarāṇāmanīkaṃ citraṃ ketuṃ janitā tvā jajāna /
24.13.3.i.d: विश्वेषां ह्यध्वराणामनीकं चित्रं केतुं जनिता त्वा जजान ।
24.13.3.i.m: "For the creator generated you as the front, the bright beacon of all sacrifices;

24.13.3.j.s: sa ā yajasva nṛvatīranu kṣāḥ spārhā iṣaḥ kṣumatīrviśvajanyāḥ //
24.13.3.j.d: स आ यजस्व नृवतीरनु क्षाः स्पार्हा इषः क्षुमतीर्विश्वजन्याः ॥
24.13.3.j.m: so offer, along the lands, desirable, rich in cattle, universal refreshments full of heroes!

24.13.3.k.s: yaṃ tvā dyāvāpṛthivī yaṃ tvāpastvaṣṭā yaṃ tvā sujanimā jajāna /
24.13.3.k.d: यं त्वा द्यावापृथिवी यं त्वापस्त्वष्टा यं त्वा सुजनिमा जजान ।
24.13.3.k.m: You whom Heaven and Earth, you whom the Waters, you whom Tvaṣṭṛ, good at generating, generated:

24.13.3.l.s: panthāmanu pravidvānpitṛyāṇaṃ dyumadagne samidhāno vi bhāhītyetasya sūktasya ṣaṭ sarvaṃ vā //
24.13.3.l.d: पन्थामनु प्रविद्वान्पितृयाणं द्युमदग्ने समिधानो वि भाहीत्येतस्य सूक्तस्य षट् सर्वं वा ॥
24.13.3.l.m: knowing well the path traversed by the fathers, O Agni, being kindled, shine brightly!"—six [verses] or the whole of this hymn;

24.13.3.m.s: viśve devāḥ śāstana mā yatheha hotā vṛto manavai yanniṣadya /
24.13.3.m.d: विश्वे देवाः शास्तन मा यथेह होता वृतो मनवै यन्निषद्य ।
24.13.3.m.m: "All you gods, instruct me how, chosen as hotṛ here, having sat down, I may think!

24.13.3.n.s: pra me brūta bhāgadheyaṃ yathā vo yena pathā havyamā vo vahāni //
24.13.3.n.d: प्र मे ब्रूत भागधेयं यथा वो येन पथा हव्यमा वो वहानि ॥
24.13.3.n.m: Declare to me your portion, as it is, along which path I may convey the oblation to you!"

24.13.3.o.m: "The one whom I desire with my mind, this very one has arrived, knowing the sacrifice, perceptive of its joints;

24.13.3.p.s: sa no yakṣaddevatātā yajīyānni hi ṣatsadantaraḥ pūrvo asmanniṣadya //
24.13.3.p.d: स नो यक्षद्देवताता यजीयान्नि हि षत्सदन्तरः पूर्वो अस्मन्निषद्य ॥
24.13.3.p.m: may he, being a better sacrificer, sacrifice for us in the godhead, for he has sat down within, ahead of us, having taken his seat!"

24.13.3.q.s: tadadya vācaḥ prathamaṃ masīya yenāsurām̐ abhi devā asāma //
24.13.3.q.d: तदद्य वाचः प्रथमं मसीय येनासुराम्̐ अभि देवा असाम ॥
24.13.3.q.m: "Today may I meditate on that first [utterance] of speech whereby we gods may overcome the asuras;

24.13.3.r.s: ūrjāda uta yajñiyāsaḥ pañca janā mama hotraṃ juṣadhvam //
24.13.3.r.d: ऊर्जाद उत यज्ञियासः पञ्च जना मम होत्रं जुषध्वम् ॥
24.13.3.r.m: eating invigorating food and worthy of sacrifice, O five peoples, enjoy my hotṛ's office!"

24.13.3.s.s: namo mahadbhyo namo arbhakebhyo namo yuvabhyo nama āśinebhyaḥ /
24.13.3.s.d: नमो महद्भ्यो नमो अर्भकेभ्यो नमो युवभ्यो नम आशिनेभ्यः ।
24.13.3.s.m: "Homage to the great, homage to the small, homage to the young, homage to the elders!

24.13.3.t.s: yajāma devānyadi śaknavāma mā jyāyasaḥ śaṃsamā vṛkṣi devā iti
24.13.3.t.d: यजाम देवान्यदि शक्नवाम मा ज्यायसः शंसमा वृक्षि देवा इति
24.13.3.t.m: Let us sacrifice to the gods if we are able; let me not, O gods, cut off the praise of the elder!"

24.13.4.a.m: Having murmured this, he causes [the adhvaryu and the pratiprasthātṛ] to take up the two ladles.

24.13.5.a.m: Everywhere before the consecratory verse, having uttered 'ye yajāmahe', he applies the sacred utterances.

24.13.6.a.m: He does not pronounce 'ye yajāmahe' at the after-offerings.

24.13.7.a.m: He recites the consecratory verses for the after-offerings without breathing in;

24.13.8.a.m: An invitatory verse has its characteristic mark at the beginning;

24.13.8.b.m: a consecratory verse has its characteristic mark at the end;

24.13.9.a.m: The invitatory verse has its characteristic mark at both ends, and likewise the consecratory verse, say some.

24.13.10.a.m: Standing, he recites the invitatory verse;

24.13.11.a.s: sā ha tvai samṛddhā puro'nuvākyā yāmabhivyāharandevatāmevāgre 'bhivyāharati /
24.13.11.a.d: सा ह त्वै समृद्धा पुरोऽनुवाक्या यामभिव्याहरन्देवतामेवाग्रे ऽभिव्याहरति ।
24.13.11.a.m: That indeed is an accomplished invitatory verse in reciting which he mentions the deity first;

24.13.11.b.s: sā ha tvai samṛddhā yājyā yasyai devatāyā adhi vaṣaṭkaroti
24.13.11.b.d: सा ह त्वै समृद्धा याज्या यस्यै देवताया अधि वषट्करोति
24.13.11.b.m: that indeed is an accomplished consecratory verse for whose deity he utters the vaṣaṭ-call.

24.13.12.a.m: He places the sacred syllable om in the verse, except for the consecratory verse.

24.14.1.a.m: Some say it is a modification of the final syllable.

24.14.2.a.m: Another [view] is that it should be an additional [syllable].

24.14.3.b.s: ṛcamuktvā praṇautyaparāmuktvā praṇautyadhike punaretadupapadyate saṃtatamṛcā vaṣaṭkarotīti ca tadvadyājyāyā adhi vaṣaṭkaroti
24.14.3.b.d: ऋचमुक्त्वा प्रणौत्यपरामुक्त्वा प्रणौत्यधिके पुनरेतदुपपद्यते संततमृचा वषट्करोतीति च तद्वद्याज्याया अधि वषट्करोति
24.14.3.b.m: “Having spoken a verse, he pronounces the praṇava; having spoken another, he pronounces the praṇava.” But this is possible only if it is additional. And likewise [the text says]: “He utters the vaṣaṭ-call continuously with the verse;” [thus] he utters the vaṣaṭ-call over the consecratory verse.

24.14.4.a.m: “Raising the voice, he utters the vaṣaṭ-call”: [this means] loudness of the sound.

24.14.5.a.s: yaṃ kāmayeta pramāyukaḥ syāditi tasyoccairapagūrya nikhidanniva vaṣaṭkuryāt /
24.14.5.a.d: यं कामयेत प्रमायुकः स्यादिति तस्योच्चैरपगूर्य निखिदन्निव वषट्कुर्यात् ।
24.14.5.a.m: For one whom he might wish to die soon, he should utter the vaṣaṭ-call having raised [his voice] loudly, as if pressing down.

24.14.5.b.s: yaṃ kāmayeta pāpīyānsyāditi nīcaistarāṃ tasya yājyāyā vaṣaṭkuryāt /
24.14.5.b.d: यं कामयेत पापीयान्स्यादिति नीचैस्तरां तस्य याज्याया वषट्कुर्यात् ।
24.14.5.b.m: For one whom he might wish to become worse off, he should utter the vaṣaṭ-call lower than his consecratory verse.

24.14.5.c.s: yaṃ kāmayeta vasīyānsyādityuccaistarāṃ tasya yājyāyā vaṣaṭkuryāt /
24.14.5.c.d: यं कामयेत वसीयान्स्यादित्युच्चैस्तरां तस्य याज्याया वषट्कुर्यात् ।
24.14.5.c.m: For one whom he might wish to become better off, he should utter the vaṣaṭ-call higher than his consecratory verse.

24.14.5.d.s: na vasīyānna pāpīyāniti samaṃ tasya yājyāyā vaṣaṭkuryāt /
24.14.5.d.d: न वसीयान्न पापीयानिति समं तस्य याज्याया वषट्कुर्यात् ।
24.14.5.d.m: [If he wishes that he be] neither better off nor worse off, he should utter the vaṣaṭ-call at the same level as his consecratory verse.

24.14.5.e.m: It is known [from scripture]: “For one desiring heaven, he should utter the vāsaṭ-call loudly, like a krauñca bird.”

24.14.6.a.m: Likewise [in the passage]: “He utters the vaṣaṭ-call louder than the verse.”

24.14.7.a.s: yaṃ devatāṃ yajettāṃ manasā dhyāyetpurā vaṣaṭkārātsvargakāmasyeti vijñāyate
24.14.7.a.d: यं देवतां यजेत्तां मनसा ध्यायेत्पुरा वषट्कारात्स्वर्गकामस्येति विज्ञायते
24.14.7.a.m: It is known [from scripture]: “Whichever deity he sacrifices to, he should meditate on that [deity] in his mind before the vaṣaṭ-call, for one who desires heaven.”

24.14.8.a.m: Having uttered the vaṣaṭ-call, he should breathe in, breathe out, and blink.

24.14.9.a.m: It is known [from scripture]: “He should sustain in-breath with out-breath, and the eye by blinking.”

24.14.10.a.m: For one whom he hates, he should utter the vaṣaṭ-call as ‘oṣaṭ’.

24.14.12.a.s: vaṣaṭkāra mā me pra vāṅmo ahaṃ tvāṃ bṛhatā mana upahvaye /
24.14.12.a.d: वषट्कार मा मे प्र वाङ्मो अहं त्वां बृहता मन उपह्वये ।
24.14.12.a.m: “O vaṣaṭ-call, do not destroy my speech, nor I you; I summon you with the bṛhat metre, O Mind!

24.14.12.b.s: na māṃ na me vācaṃ hinasāt /
24.14.12.b.d: न मां न मे वाचं हिनसात् ।
24.14.12.b.m: May it not injure me, nor my speech!

24.14.12.c.d: हव्यं देवेभ्यो ऽभिवहाम्योजः सहः सह ओजः ।
24.14.12.c.m: I carry the oblation to the gods, vigor, strength, strength, vigor!”

24.14.12.d.s: vāgvaṣaṭkāra namaste astu mā mā hiṃsīrityetadvaṣaṭkṛte japati /
24.14.12.d.d: वाग्वषट्कार नमस्ते अस्तु मा मा हिंसीरित्येतद्वषट्कृते जपति ।
24.14.12.d.m: “O Speech, O vaṣaṭ-call, homage be to you; do not injure me!”—having uttered the vaṣaṭ-call, he mutters this [formula].

24.14.12.e.s: vāgvaṣaṭkāra namaste astu mā mā hiṃsīriti vā
24.14.12.e.d: वाग्वषट्कार नमस्ते अस्तु मा मा हिंसीरिति वा
24.14.12.e.m: Or [only]: “O Speech, O vaṣaṭ-call, homage be to you; do not injure me!”

24.14.13.a.s: aṅgulī muktvā miṣe prāṇāyeti mukhadeśamūrdhvamutkṛṣyorje 'pānāyetyavācīnaṃ niyacchati
24.14.13.a.d: अङ्गुली मुक्त्वा मिषे प्राणायेति मुखदेशमूर्ध्वमुत्कृष्योर्जे ऽपानायेत्यवाचीनं नियच्छति
24.14.13.a.m: Having unclasped his fingers, having raised [them] upward toward the mouth with [the words]: “For sap, for in-breath,” he directs [them] downward with [the words]: “For vigor, for out-breath.”

24.14.14.a.m: Holding the cut-off intermediate iḍā with the fingers, he does not make a fist.

24.14.15.a.m: He invokes it facing as if toward his mouth.

24.14.16.a.m: It has been said: “For one whom he might wish to be without cattle, [he should invoke] it turned away.”

24.14.17.a.m: However, [there is] a prohibition against repetition of words.

24.14.18.a.m: And it is known [from scripture]: “ ‘The iḍā is invoked’—that is turned away;

24.14.19.a.d: आध्वर्यव एवातो ऽन्यानि कर्माणि होतुराम्नातानि भवन्ति ।
24.14.19.a.m: Henceforth, other rites prescribed for the hotṛ belong solely to the adhvaryu's duties.

24.14.19.b.m: Other [rites are assigned to] other [priests] by express teaching.
